Personal forgiveness is a most powerful experience. Properly accepted, it will change your life, it will make you better and it will provoke you to be forgiving in the same way that you are forgiven. But, personal forgiveness is only the beginning, the introduction, the prelude to what the forgiveness of the cross brought to us. You see, there are a myriad of prophecies that speak of worldwide restitution, worldwide peace and harmony – these are the real stories of the cross.

Personal forgiveness is good, but these prophecies fulfilled are even better!

Daniel 2:44: (ASV) And in the days of those kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom which shall never be destroyed, nor shall the sovereignty thereof be left to another people; but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.

There is a very specific context being set out here in Daniel. We have …those kings – what kings? The kings of the earth. We have the God of heaven setting up an indestructible kingdom that breaks the previous kingdoms in pieces, so it must be, again, here on the earth.

Jesus actually taught us to pray for this in the Lord’s Prayer: thy Kingdom come, thy will be done, in earth as it is in heaven. Think about how much sense this makes: Jesus died for Adam, and therefore for us, and that means he came to restore what was lost…a perfect earth!

Colossians 1:18-20: (NRSV) 18He is the head of the body, the church; he is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that he might come to have first place in everything. 19For in him all the fullness of God was pleased to dwell, 20and through him God was pleased to reconcile to himself all things, whether on earth or in heaven, by making peace through the blood of his cross.

Again notice the elements here: We have Jesus and the Church, his called-out ones. Then it says that God through Jesus and his sacrifice reconciled and made peace with ALL things – this is much more than the true Church. The blood of the cross is about much more than me – it is about us – ALL of us!

Acts 3:20-21: (NASB) 20and that He may send Jesus, the Christ appointed for you, 21whom heaven must receive until the period of restoration of all things about which God spoke by the mouth of His holy prophets from ancient time.

God through Jesus is not only reconciling all things to Himself, He is restoring all things. When you restore something, you return it to its former state. Peter here in Acts says that all of the prophets spoke of this restoration. Here are just a few:

Isaiah 51:3: (NRSV) 3For the LORD will comfort Zion; he will comfort all her waste places, and will make her wilderness like Eden, her desert like the garden of the LORD; joy and gladness will be found in her, thanksgiving and the voice of song.

The perfection of Eden was lost, and Isaiah is saying that the waste places of earth will look like it? See, redemption brings restitution and restitution brings gladness, thanksgiving and song. How do we know? The prophecies tell us!

Micah 4:1-5: (KJV) 1But in the last days it shall come to pass, that the mountain of the house of the LORD shall be established in the top of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills; and people shall flow unto it. 2And many nations shall come, and say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for the law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

These are specifics about the future of earth! There will be many nations. They will ALL be seeking after God which indicates that they must go through a learning curve. They will walk in Godly paths with Israel as their example. 3And he shall judge among many people, and rebuke strong nations afar off; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more. 4But they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid: for the mouth of the LORD of hosts hath spoken it. 5For all people will walk every one in the name of his god, and we will walk in the name of the LORD our God for ever and ever.

God will teach the world the ways of peace: swords to plowshares, spears to pruning hooks, no more war, rather they will all dwell in peace – each with the ability to provide for themselves and all while living under God! This is the direct result of the sacrifice of the cross – the ransom payment for Adam and his sin. This is the way God intended this world to be!

So, while those now faithful to Jesus will have an inheritance in heaven, the “everybody else” will have an inheritance on earth…once they prove their faithfulness to Jesus in the Judgment Day.

Praise be to God for his unspeakable gift!

No wonder the scripture says…

Philippians 2:8-11: (NASB) 8Being found in appearance as a man, he humbled himself by becoming obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross. 9For this reason also, God highly exalted him, and bestowed on him the name which is above every name, 10so that at the name of Jesus every knee will bow...11and that every tongue will confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

What a comprehensive picture of the simple yet profound work of Jesus. Adam sinned, therefore we all sin and justice required satisfaction. Jesus came, lived perfectly, gave that life up and therefore satisfied justice. He now reigns on high and all of the world under the curse of Adam will be given a new lease on life – why? Because that is what justice demands!

Isaiah 65:21-25: (NRSV) 21They shall build houses and inhabit them; they shall plant vineyards and eat their fruit. 22They shall not build and another inhabit; they shall not plant and another eat; for like the days of a tree shall the days of my people be, and my chosen shall long enjoy the work of their hands. 23They shall not labor in vain, or bear children for calamity; for they shall be offspring blessed by the LORD-- and their descendants as well. 24Before they call I will answer, while they are yet speaking I will hear. 25The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, the lion shall eat straw like the ox; but the serpent--its food shall be dust! They shall not hurt or destroy on all My holy mountain, says the LORD.

This is yet another example of a clear picture of an amazing earthly setting. Building houses, planting vineyards, personal responsibility, not laboring in vain, the Almighty guiding and directing the affairs of earth. The wolf and the lamb will feed together.

Yes, the sacrifice of Jesus…that is what bought this future!

No wonder Revelation 21:4 says: And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.

Isaiah 35:5-10: (NRSV) 5Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped; 6then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the speechless sing for joy. For waters shall break forth in the wilderness, and streams in the desert; 7the burning sand shall become a pool, and the thirsty ground springs of water; the haunt of jackals shall become a swamp, the grass shall become reeds and rushes. 8A highway shall be there, and it shall be called the Holy Way; the unclean shall not travel on it but it shall be for God’s people; no traveler, not even fools, shall go astray. 9No lion shall be there, nor shall any ravenous beast come up on it; they shall not be found there, but the redeemed shall walk there. 10And the ransomed of the LORD shall return, and come to Zion with singing; everlasting joy shall be upon their heads; they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.

Psalms 145:9-13: (NRSV) 9The LORD is good to all, and his compassion is over all that he has made. 10All your works shall give thanks to you, O LORD, and all your faithful shall bless you. 11They shall speak of the glory of your kingdom, and tell of your power, 12to make known to all people your mighty deeds, and the glorious splendor of your kingdom. 13Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and your dominion endures throughout all generations. The LORD is faithful in all his words, and gracious in all his deeds.

We follow the Jewish calendar when calculating the day of the Last Supper and when Jesus hung on the cross. Today is not the actual day Jesus was raised from the tomb.

Also, you will notice we do not talk about Easter. Technically Easter is based on pagan rituals traced back to the goddess Estera, a goddess of fertility. Early Catholicism tried to combine the sacredness of Christianity with paganism in hopes of drawing Pagans to Christianity with negative results that are still felt today.

We want to make sure we are focusing on the right things. Jesus asked us at the Last Supper to do this in remembrance of me each year at this time – honoring the memorial of his body and blood, sacrificed for our benefit. We were told to focus on that simple ceremony so that we remember the core

value of his death and resurrection. This program is built upon that remembrance and his ransom price paid for all of mankind.

Jesus came forth from the grave, and restitution therefore is impossible to stop. Satan has been defeated! It is only a matter of time before his lease is up. God wins through the sacrifice of Jesus.

Jesus IS Risen!

For Jonathan and Rick and Christian Questions...

## Episode 1301 — Can We Be Content With Chaos?
Published: 2023-10-02
Episode page: https://christianquestions.com/society/1301-chaos/

James 3:17: But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits, unwavering, without hypocrisy.

Chaos rules! Just look around at the world’s social, political and moral condition. We all want what we want, and we seem to go to greater lengths than ever before to demand we have it. Having what we want doesn’t stop there, as we now more often than not demand that what I want is accepted by all. This chaos is not merely limited to our social media presence. Oh no, it expands into our perceived right to relabel any and every aspect of life as we see fit. From politics to family dynamics, to workplace expectations to educational environments, we are running towards a social order that is founded upon disorder. What are we, as Christians, supposed to do with all of this? How could these unsettling and monumental developments possibly be a part of God’s plan? It's our belief that God is a God of order. Our theme text tells us this:

James 3:17: But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits, unwavering, without hypocrisy.

This describes God's wisdom as a calming influence. And yet, God uses chaos as a tool for that calm order. How can this be? To begin to understand we need to first understand chaos.

Merriam Webster Dictionary: Chaos: noun 1a: a state of utter confusion 1b: a confused mass or mixture 2a: a state of things in which chance is supreme 2b: the inherent unpredictability in the behavior of a complex natural system (such as the atmosphere, boiling water, or the beating heart) Chaos can mean complete disorder, but it can also mean a disorder that is beyond our capacity to understand or measure.

Deterministic Chaos, How Chaos Theory Unravels the Mysteries of Nature, Seeker - Deterministic chaos: See, as humans, we're always trying to know more about how our world works. So, we make models. For example, we have the bowling ball. We know the weight of the bowling ball, the effective gravity, the density of the air, the height of the balcony from which the bowling ball is to be dropped. And we can put all those things together into a system of equations that we can use to tell us things like, how fast the bowling ball would fall, or the force with which it would impact the ground. That means we can also reasonably predict what might happen if any of those variables were to change. This is a “deterministic system.” The behavior of certain variables is determined by their known characteristics, but not a lot of the world is like the bowling ball example. It's a whole lot messier.

This is talking about a system in which mathematics can predict the deterministic system. This is important. Predicting weather is all about the mathematics of deterministic chaos. This will help us understand the bigger picture of chaos, because chaos comes to us in different ways.

First, we have a deterministic chaos that is strictly designed by God. We will call this planned chaos. In this kind of chaos, things SEEM to be out of order and out of control, but they are, in fact, precisely as God designed them to be.

The single greatest example of this is creation:

Genesis 1:1-5: 1 In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. 2 The earth was formless and void, and darkness was over the surface of the deep… To the untrained eye, the chaos and harshness of this beginning stage would make no sense. How can we possibly get all of the diverse and detailed life the earth brought forth out of that?

From our perspective, the finished earth is so far off from this description, we wouldn’t be able to see how to go from there to here with all the incredible detail and beauty of all the things on the earth.

From God’s perspective, this was His designed starting point. His planned chaos was simply a beginning point, as it held all of His predetermined and necessary ingredients to make the earth habitable. When we look at this planned chaos, it looks out of control, but God is saying, Wait! Just let Me finish… …and the spirit of God was moving over the surface of the waters. 3 Then God said, Let there be light; and there was light. 4 God saw that the light was good; and God separated the light from the darkness. 5 God called the light day, and the darkness He called night. And there was evening and there was morning, one day.

We are taking this small clip of creation as an example of God’s planned chaos. Out of a seemingly dark and senseless mass of elements, God created the systems of our earth! The fact that creation is still going on in the universe while it continues to expand is amazing. Is that just by chance? We think not.

To see all of these things continuing to unfold and to say there is no power behind them is just absurd. We do not understand how God created the universe, and we do not have to! It is bigger than we are, and it is His planned chaos.

Along with God’s planned chaos, chaos also comes to us by way of God’s permission. This kind of chaos contains elements that are not of God’s direct creation but are results of God’s planned permission of evil and sin. We will call this God’s permitted chaos. To the untrained eye, this kind of chaos is scary, as its elements cannot be so easily traced

back to a clear and definitive design plan. However, as we shall see, this brand of chaos is in the end always subject to the eternal will, power and wisdom of God. This chaos is brewing and has evil and darkness in it. God did not build the evil and darkness, but He can USE the evil and darkness within His grand plan to allow chaos to exist for a reason. We will be spending most of our time on permitted chaos. There are many great examples of this permitted chaos.

In chapter 1 of his prophecy, Habakkuk was given a disturbing vision of how the Chaldeans would overrun God’s people:

Habakkuk 1:2-4: 2 How long, O LORD, will I call for help, and You will not hear? I cry out to You, Violence! Yet You do not save. 3 Why do You make me see iniquity, and cause me to look on wickedness? Yes, destruction and violence are before me; strife exists and contention arises. 4 Therefore the law is ignored and justice is never upheld. For the wicked surround the righteous; therefore justice comes out perverted.

Habakkuk is distraught. He's crying, Lord, where are You? Don't you see what's happening? This seemed senseless to Habakkuk. Why wasn’t God stepping in and averting this chaos? We can all get to that exact point. We look at the chaos in the world around us and ask, Where is God? Doesn’t He see? This question has been asked for ages and generations because darkness and sin are always godless. But if they are godless and this is God’s creation, how do these two opposing sides fit together? HOLD ON, let God finish! After Habakkuk poured out his fears to God, he then waited for God’s response:

Habakkuk 2:1-3: 1 I will stand on my guard post and station myself on the rampart; and I will keep watch to see what He will speak to me, and how I may reply when I am reproved. 2 Then the LORD answered me and said, Record the vision and inscribe it on tablets, that the one who reads it may run. 3 For the vision is yet for the appointed time; it hastens toward the goal and it will not fail. Though it tarries, wait for it; for it will certainly come, it will not delay. Habakkuk knows God is going to reply to his outburst. Maybe I got a little bit over the top in my reaction when I said, God – how come You do not see!? I really know better… We are doing a little paraphrasing, but Habakkuk is told there is a vision for all of this, and he will have to wait. Even though the vision looks like it is going to take forever, it will come.

God proceeds to speak of evil and idolatry. Then in chapter 3 (that we will come back to shortly), Habakkuk sums up the glorious ending God revealed. The vision ends with an enormous lesson having to do with the chaos of the moment Habakkuk had been looking at saying, This is awful! I cannot handle this. We will come back to this later.

Does this mean God uses COVID-19, hurricanes and other disasters for His glory? God ALLOWS - within His permitted chaos - COVID-19, natural disasters and so forth, for His glory. He allows these because He allows the unraveling of things in order to show the sinfulness of sin. These are all pieces of the chaotic puzzle that so many of us look at and ask, Where is God? HOLD ON – let Him finish! This is God’s permitted chaos we are beginning to look at and hopefully beginning to appreciate. Chaos is BIG! Chaos is everywhere! But not to worry, because God already knows and already has His planned outcomes for everything!

If God does have a grip on all of the world’s big-picture chaos, how do we get a grip on our own chaos experiences?

As Christians, it is important we put our life experiences AND our life observations in their appropriate perspective. Whether the chaos that affects us comes from our small circle of influence or bigger social or world events, it needs clarity. This clarity can only come when we realize our fundamental reactions to chaos can increase or decrease its power.

We either react to the chaos by feeding it or by defusing it. Chaos can have greater power because of us or less power because of us. We have some responsibility. Are we overwhelmed by chaos because it displays large-scale lack of control, or are we overwhelmed by chaos due to our own personal lack of knowledge or faith? It could be a combination of the two, but these are two big concerns.

This next letter from the Apostle Paul was written from prison. He was under house arrest. How did he handle that chaos?

Philippians 4:10-13: 10 But I rejoiced in the Lord greatly, that now at last you have revived your concern for me; indeed, you were concerned before, but you lacked opportunity. 11 Not that I speak from want, for I have learned to be content in whatever circumstances I am. 12 I know how to get along with humble means, and I also know how to live in prosperity; in any and every circumstance I have learned the secret of being filled and going hungry, both of having abundance and suffering need. 13 I can do all things through him who strengthens me.

Despite Paul sitting in prison, he was rejoicing! He was unable to do what he was supposed to do, so why was he happy? Because he had learned the secret, even though his life was dramatically different in prison.

Chaos Clarifier: Learn the secret that the Apostle Paul learned. Know that we can do all things through Christ and not through our own strength or perception. This is easy to say but hard to do. Saying it is a nice gesture, but doing it is life-changing. I can do all things - the Apostle Paul showed us how. I can be stifled. It is okay because it is in God’s hands. I will do the best I can within this little opportunity versus the great opportunity of traveling over the continent preaching. There was a great difference in his circumstances, but he did not look at it as less of an opportunity. The chaos was clarified and therefore handleable.

It is not enough to just say it; we have to do it.

Chaos may arise on our part when we find ourselves in circumstances of potential physical harm or danger. This is permitted chaos. In God’s permitted chaos, He allows sin, darkness and bad things to be mixed in for the ultimate good.

This permitted chaos in and of itself creates havoc because it brings uncertainty. What happens next? Internal chaos. This internal chaos provokes us to react, and that usually means panic.

We all go through that panic scenario when we just don’t know what to do and it seems too much to handle.

The Weather, How Chaos Theory Unravels the Mysteries of Nature, Seeker - Take the weather: just think about all the things that go into making weather - temperatures, humidity, wind strength and direction, rotation of the earth; the list is exhaustive. We do have models for how all these many variables behave, but a perfect weather prediction would require highly accurate measurements of all the many contributing variables over every square inch of the piece of atmosphere we’re looking at. In a system like this, little measurement errors can result in huge fluctuations of our calculated result. Tiny changes of the input mean a large variation of the output. Now don't get me wrong, the system is still deterministic. The variables behave the way we expect them to based on their physical properties. So, it's quite different from something that is random, but it's highly unpredictable and subject to vast variation. The system may look disorganized, but there is a set of rules that apply to the chaos - deterministic chaos.

Looking at the permitted chaos of God in His plan, the system may look disorganized, but it has rules; it is deterministic. This is important. Weather forecasts are seldom right because the variables are incredibly massive. We can only predict out so far without the models breaking down. We can’t account for every little variable.

Let’s look at permitted chaos examples in God’s plan.

Jesus was with his disciples after a normal day of preaching to the masses:

Mark 4:33-36: 33 With many such parables he was speaking the word to them, so far as they were able to hear it; 34 and he did not speak to them without a parable; but he was explaining everything privately to his own disciples. 35 On that day, when evening came, he said to them, Let us go over to the other side. 36 Leaving the crowd, they took him along with them in the boat, just as he was; and other boats were with him.

Chaos is most difficult when there is no warning:

Mark 4:37-38: 37 And there arose a fierce gale of wind, and the waves were breaking over the boat so much that the boat was already filling up. 38 Jesus himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion; and they woke him and said to him, Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?

The waves were breaking over the boat so much that the boat was already filling up with water. From a human standpoint, this is justifiable panic. Mere humans are no match for the elements!

Mark 4:39-41: 39 And he got up and rebuked the wind and said to the sea, Hush (Peace), be still. And the wind died down and it became perfectly calm. 40 And he said to them, Why are you afraid? Do you still have no faith? 41 They became very much afraid and said to one another, who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?

Jesus’ lesson was, I am with you; therefore, you are safe. It is by the power of God’s own spirit that Jesus was able to perform this amazing, natural miracle of calming the sea and taking that fear instantly away.

Chaos Clarifier: We are NO match for the elements, but God’s power through Jesus can and will protect us as He sees fit. To be no match for the elements is therefore of no consequence. Just be smart! Just stand in faith!

In other words, use a spirit of a sound mind. Don't go outside during a tornado and say, “I have Jesus,” thinking you will be safe. That’s just foolish!

We were visiting our son over the last few days in Virginia at the beach. The waves were unusually large because of tropical storms out in the Atlantic Ocean. There were five, six foot waves and seemed huge. We were up near the beach and looking at them.

The waves roll in and don’t care what is in front of them. The power and strength were overwhelming! It was easy for us because we were standing on solid ground and could just walk away from the sea.

For the disciples, though, those massive waves were crashing into their boat. We can imagine the great fear they had.

It would not have been smart for us to just walk out into the water and say, “We have Jesus, so we need not worry about the waves!” No, we stayed on solid ground and didn’t go out too far into the water because that would be foolish. This particular chaos for the disciples was handled by God’s spirit in His way.

This permitted chaos can easily bring high emotion and gut reactions of aggression that are NOT godly. The betrayal of Jesus in the Garden of Gethsemane is a good example of this.

The following are the combined accounts of all four gospels - Matthew, Mark, Luke and John. We will summarize some details:

Luke 22:47: …and the one called Judas, one of the twelve, was preceding them…

Mark 14:44: 44 Now he who was betraying him had given them a signal, saying, whomever I kiss, he is the one; seize him and lead him away under guard.

Luke 22:47,48: 47 …and he approached Jesus to kiss him. 48 But Jesus said to him, Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?

Matthew 26:49-50: 49 Immediately Judas went to Jesus and said, Hail, Rabbi! and kissed him. 50 And Jesus said to him, Friend, do what you have come for…

Summing up John 18:4-9: Jesus approached the oncoming crowd and identified himself as the one they were seeking. The crowd fell back when Jesus spoke. Power forced them to the ground. Jesus proved they had no power over him.

Tensions were building and there was the chaos of Judas actually betraying Jesus right in front of the other apostles.

Jesus then reasoned with the crowd to let his disciples go:

Luke 22:49: When those who were around him (the apostles) saw what was going to happen, they said, Lord, shall we strike with the sword?

Matthew 26:50: …Then they came and laid hands on Jesus and seized him.

John 18:10-11: 10 Simon Peter then, having a sword, drew it and struck the high priest's slave, and cut off his right ear; and the slave's name was Malchus. 11 So Jesus said to Peter…

Luke 22:51: …Stop! No more of this…

John 18:11: …Put the sword into the sheath…

Matthew 26:52-54: 52 for all those who take up the sword shall perish by the sword. 53 Or do you think that I cannot appeal to my Father, and He will at once put at my disposal more than twelve legions of angels? 54 How then will the Scriptures be fulfilled, which say that it must happen this way?

John 18:11: …the cup which the Father has given me, shall I not drink it?

There is so much happening! The crowd approaches Jesus, and the disciples ask, Shall we strike with the sword? Of course, Peter doesn’t wait for an answer; he just attacks because that’s Peter. Chaos breaks out. There is all-out violence beginning with that first stroke of the sword starting a violent interchange.

Jesus, just like he did with the sea, says, Stop; no more of this. This is something I am here to accept and embrace because it is my Father’s will. What looks like chaos to you is God’s permitted chaos to me, and I am willing to walk through it and with it. The apostles’ reaction was human and justifiable: Jesus was innocent, so there was no way they would let the soldiers take him!

Chaos had begun to erupt, but Jesus took control and diffused it.

In the middle of diffusing that chaos, what happened next?

Luke 22:51: …And he touched his ear and healed him.

Here is how Jesus looked at this moment of permitted chaos in God’s plan. Not only did he stop the violence, but he reversed the results of the violence because they were unjustifiable. It was one of his own people hurting someone else. He healed the soldier. It gives us an amazing sense of the depth of Jesus’ character.

Chaos Clarifier: When we are faced with clear injustice, we need to remember what Jesus did. He saw God’s direction and followed it without hesitation.

But Jesus understood that injustice was a necessary permitted chaos in order to give glory to God. We need to remember this. Be like our Lord.

Matthew 26:55-56: 55 At that time Jesus said to the crowds, Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest me as you would against a robber? Every day I used to sit in the temple teaching and you did not seize me. 56 But all this has taken place to fulfill the Scriptures of the prophets…

Luke 22:53: …but this hour and the power of darkness are yours.

Matthew 26:56: …Then all the disciples left him and fled.

John 18:12: (KJV) Then the band and the captain and officers of the Jews took Jesus, and bound him.

The chaos continued because now all Jesus’ disciples fled. They were in a chaotic state, but Jesus was calm in the midst of this permitted chaos.

This is an important question because we are not going to get away from chaos. Are we going to respond in a Jesus-like manner and submit to whatever God’s pemitted chaos brings to us? It is becoming ever more obvious that there is no getting away from chaos. How we handle all that chaos is the real issue!

Repelling the temptation to react to chaos that comes from circumstances is one thing. How do we handle our own ability to create chaos?

Our next examples will focus on how we, as human beings, can manufacture chaos based on our own imperfect thoughts and emotions. While those creating the chaos in these next examples were not Christians, we want to be sure to understand they were humans, just like we are. Let’s be guarded against our own humanity!

An example is the zealots in Israel in Jesus’ day. They were trying to push the envelope to provoke a military rebellion against the Romans. Some believe Judas, with his false perceived ideas, may have tried to push Jesus into taking over as Messiah. Most of Israel was expecting Messiah to take control over Rome. When Judas realized Jesus didn't resist arrest, Judas hung himself.

What about a modern-day example?

There are lots of modern-day examples. The key to it all is drama and gaining attention. This is unfortunate because we take things into our own hands. In a recent article, some people decided that they were going to dramatically stop traffic, so they glued their hands to the road so that nobody could get past. What was their point? They thought they were making a dramatic statement forcing others to stop and listen, but it just seemed foolish. What if somebody was sick or dying, or an ambulance had to get somewhere? If we need to resort to drama and creating chaos, maybe our point is not the point it should be.

Christians can create chaos! This is not a good idea.

This is not a state of mind that can easily be diffused. When Paul and Barnabas were in Iconium, they preached the gospel and performed miracles and drew many Jews and Greeks to them. Some from a Jewish sect of that city stirred non-believers against them and sought to stone them. Paul and Barnabas left the city.

Chaos Clarifier: Paul and Barnabas understood this circumstance was not going to bring glory to God and wisely moved on. Are we as wise and perceptive in our moments of chaos?

They diffused the situation and found a way out.

When they went to Lystra, Paul healed a lame man who had faith. This public healing caused exactly the opposite reaction from the previous Greek crowds:

Acts 14:11-13: 11 When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they raised their voice, saying in the Lycaonian language, The gods have become like men and have come down to us. 12 And they began calling Barnabas, Zeus, and Paul, Hermes, because he was the chief speaker. 13 The priest of Zeus, whose temple was just outside the city, brought oxen and garlands to the gates, and wanted to offer sacrifice with the crowds.

Which is worse: the chaos of people trying to stone you to death, or the chaos of people proclaiming you as false gods to worship? We can’t imagine how much frustration that caused Paul and Barnabas who were messengers of the gospel of Jesus Christ. This is not what they were there for.

Acts 14:14-15: 14 But when the apostles, Barnabas and Paul heard of it, they tore their robes and rushed out into the crowd, crying out 15 and saying, Men, why are you doing these things? We are also men of the same nature as you, and preach the gospel to you that you should turn from these vain things to a living God…

Here was chaos breaking out in a different way. This chaos was, We want to laud you and call you a god versus the chaos of We want to kill you. Both of these are crowd reactions, and crowd reactions are an element of chaos that can become unpredictable. Paul and Barnabas explained how God was the Creator of all things and was bigger than their manmade idols, and how He is reflected in nature. They emphatically said, We are NOT gods! The crowd was starting to calm down a little bit. But look what happened: Chaos escalated:

Acts 14:18-20: 18 Even saying these things, with difficulty they restrained the crowds from offering sacrifice to them. 19 But Jews came from Antioch and Iconium, and having won over the crowds, they stoned Paul and dragged him out of the city, supposing him to be dead. 20 But while the disciples stood around him, he got up and entered the city. The next day he went away with Barnabas to Derbe.

How is it possible that the crowd could be “won over” by the Jews from Antioch after Paul performed a miracle from the power of God?

It seems there are missing pieces here. It is not written what actually happened, but we can speculate. These Jews from Antioch and Iconium didn't like Paul. They were not idolaters themselves, but they came to this city, followed Paul and saw what he was doing. It’s possible they told the crowd wanting to worship Paul something like, You realize what he's doing, don't you? He's taking your gods away! He's saying what you've worshiped for your whole life, what your parents have worshiped and their parents have worshiped, is just a piece of stone. Are you going to let him get away with that? Do you see how insulting this is? They riled up the emotions of the crowd and created this chaos to the point of stoning him and leaving him for dead. Then the disciples gather around him, he stands up, shakes himself off and walks back into the city. This is our beloved Apostle Paul. We can see the chaos from the crowds and the pathetic rivalry that drove the individuals to such high levels of action.

Chaos Clarifier: Whether we perpetrate this chaotic rivalry or are the victims of it, we need to understand that our human emotions easily block reason and kindness when we feel threatened.

When we hear the word “rivalry,” the first thing we might think of is politics. It is so nasty in our world today. With politics, we start out with our ideology. Having an ideology is good because it defines the way life and society should be. This develops a very strong sense of right and wrong. That sense of right and wrong then develops into labeling those who see it differently. That labeling then becomes rivalry. And that rivalry then can become chaotic because we take it out of context.

Instead of saying, These human beings are just like me; they have opinions that are thought out just like me. Oh no, we don't do that. Instead we say, They are a bunch of idiots. They don't know what they are talking about and don’t understand. We create this massive problem, making chaos bigger.

We have to be careful not to stimulate rivalry like this because it is so ungodly.

Sometimes we cannot diffuse the chaos around us, but we can deflate the chaos within us.

How do we do this? Selah! Stop, pause and consider. Count to three. Remember where we once stood and compare it to the solid ground of the cause of Christ upon which we now stand.

We will look at several verses in the third chapter of Philippians and break it up into four different parts as we go through the rest of this episode:

Philippians 3:7-8: 7 But whatever things were gain to me, those things I have counted as loss for the sake of Christ. 8 More than that, I count all things to be loss in view of the surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord, for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and count them but rubbish so that I may gain Christ, Remember where you stood versus where you now stand as a follower of Christ. There is a difference. We need to make sure we continue to stand in the present, not in past emotions we once had.

In such cases, the reaction is fear. We can easily resort to making up stories and exaggerations about those whom we may perceive as threats.

Stephen’s final experience and death were good examples of what can happen when people let their fears overwhelm them:

Acts 6:8-15: 8 And Stephen, full of grace and power, was performing great wonders and signs among the people. 9 But some men from what was called the Synagogue of the Freedmen… rose up and argued with Stephen. 10 But they were unable to cope with the wisdom and the spirit with which he was speaking.

Being overmatched by Stephen’s reasoning did not result in humble consideration of the disagreement - just the opposite. 11 Then they secretly induced men to say, We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses and against God. 12 And they stirred up the people, the elders and the scribes, and they came up to him and dragged him away and brought him before the Council. Lies from men made Stephen look evil to others, and it picked up fierce momentum.

It is amazing how fast that kind of chaos picks up momentum. Are we contributing to that in any way? We need to be honest with ourselves, especially if we have strong political feelings. Do we find ourselves bending the truth a little bit because our opponents really do not know what they are talking about? Have we talked to these people to find out? This kind of chaotic reaction is all too common. How many times do people just want to be rid of those who stifle their own beliefs and opinions? 13 They put forward false witnesses who said, This man incessantly speaks against this holy place and the Law; 14 for we have heard him say that this Nazarene, Jesus, will destroy this place and alter the customs which Moses handed down to us. 15 And fixing their gaze on him, all who were sitting in the Council saw his face like the face of an angel. Steven showed godly peace as his response to their anger. He was backed into a corner and had nowhere to hide. He responded with godly peace.

Social media is a great way for us to fall into the creation of chaos. We don’t ever want to be part of social media that puts others down.

Another way of describing social media at its worst is called “cancel culture,” where people destroy your reputation if you don’t agree with their views.

Chaos Clarifier: How easy is it for me to short circuit the system for the sake of shielding my own beliefs from being challenged? On the other side, how bold and yet humble am I when I am being mistreated by others for the sake of the truth of Scripture?

We have two focuses:

1. If we are causing chaos, WHY are we doing it?

2. If we are receiving chaos from others, HOW are we handling it?

Sometimes we cannot diffuse the chaos around us, but we can deflate the chaos within us. How do we do this? Selah! Stop, pause and consider. Count to three. Compare whatever principles drove your past actions to the principles of Christ’s righteousness driving your present actions.

Philippians 3:9-11: 9 and may be found in him, not having a righteousness of my own derived from the Law, but that which is through faith in Christ, the righteousness which comes from God on the basis of faith, 10 that I may know him and the power of his resurrection and the fellowship of his sufferings, being conformed to his death; 11 in order that I may attain to the resurrection from the dead.

Our battle is against how we feel. Our emotions can be fragile, but we must rise above our feelings and emotions for the sake of Christlikeness. Compare the principles that used to drive us versus the principles of Christ’s righteousness presently driving us and leave the other behind. This is important. We do not want to be contributing to the chaos around us because it is not a godly contribution.

This Christlike dignity is our “chaos diffuser.” We want to have nothing less than Christlike dignity.

Which is worse? Chaos from within or chaos from the outside? Does it really matter? Let’s just focus on putting it all in its place!

We have spent time on chaos from our circumstances and chaos from our own hearts. What is the lasting, big picture of the destiny of chaos? This is the whole point of this discussion. If God is a God of order (and He is), then how does God once and for all put chaos in its rightful place? Remember Habakkuk? Before we return to his prophecy, we want to look at one example of how Jesus himself intentionally caused chaos.

After Jesus triumphantly rode into Jerusalem with the crowds hailing him as Messiah, he created chaos to send a message of righting a wrong:

Matthew 21:12-13: 12 And Jesus entered the temple and drove out all those who were buying and selling in the temple, and overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those who were selling doves. 13 And he said to them, It is written, My house shall be called a house of prayer; but you are making it a robbers’ den.

What a bold action!

Chaos Clarifier: Jesus knew the people needed to see just how far they had fallen from God’s ways. He also knew that the wrongs being done were not yet due to be corrected.

Why did Jesus do it?

Perhaps he did it to show that coming back to God for Israel and the world would have to be through God’s permitted chaos. We know Israel was being cast off. They would go through a long period of disfavor. We see God's permitted chaos had to be put in place because of their sin. Perhaps he was showing them they made the Temple a den of thieves and they would now suffer the lengthy consequences of such actions before they would be able to come back to God as a nation.

Jesus intentionally caused chaos to send a spiritual and eternal message of the value of having loyalty to God.

Chaos is everywhere, How Chaos Theory Unravels the Mysteries of Nature, Seeker - So many natural systems are chaotic — like the climate as a whole, the dynamics of clouds, population dynamics, the patterns of the stock market, the way your milk swirls into and combines with your coffee. That's chaos theory in fluid dynamics. These systems may be chaotic and have seemed impossibly daunting in the past, but the math of chaos theory is now relatively small potatoes to the huge supercomputers that we can use to calculate the progression of chaotic systems like the climate with more accuracy than ever before.

We hear the joy in the speaker’s voice that the supercomputers are cracking the case! We appreciate the leaps and bounds with which humankind has come in terms of trying to figure all of these things out. But we are trying to crack the case of the permitted chaos God has already put in place. He has made it all work and created all these systems that we are just trying to figure out. We are proud of ourselves when we discover what has always been.

Let’s look at some examples.

Chaos:

Daniel 12:1: Now at that time Michael, the great prince who stands guard over the sons of your people, will arise. And there will be a time of distress such as never occurred since there was a nation until that time; and at that time your people, everyone who is found written in the book, will be rescued.

We know the future time of distress will be scary and massive. We can’t change the fact that it is coming, but we can change our heart and mind because of the good that comes after it.

The chaos of the time of distress now brings us to the kingdom in the same book of Daniel.

Kingdom:

Daniel 2:44: In the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom which will never be destroyed, and that kingdom will not be left for another people; it will crush and put an end to all these kingdoms, but it will itself endure forever.

We need to remember God had this all planned from before sin entered into the picture with Adam. Revelation 13:8 says Jesus was the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world. No matter how difficult it may be, God's kingdom will be the silver lining. We started out this episode looking at the deterministic chaos of creation. Even before the chaos, God had the solution. He had determined what would happen, so the solution was already in place. This should give us great calm.

Sometimes we cannot diffuse the chaos around us, but we can deflate the chaos within us. How do we do this? Selah! Stop, pause and consider. Count to three. Press forward. What happens around us does not determine what happens within us unless we allow it to.

Philippians 3:12: Not that I have already obtained it or have already become perfect, but I press on so that I may lay hold of that for which also I was laid hold of by Christ Jesus. Press on. We can hold onto God’s promises that we know are future because God said they would happen, even when the present looks very dark.

Chaos:

Psalms 46:1-3: 1 God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. 2 Therefore we will not fear, though the earth should change and though the mountains (symbolically representing governments) slip into the heart of the sea; 3 Though its waters roar and foam (symbolically representing the restless masses of humanity), though the mountains quake at its swelling pride. Selah.

Pause and consider – count to three because that sounds pretty dramatic! We have that selah moment, but a few verses down in the same Psalm we have: Kingdom:

Psalms 46:9-11: 9 He makes wars to cease to the end of the earth; He breaks the bow and cuts the spear in two; He burns the chariots with fire. 10 Cease striving and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted in the earth. 11 The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold. Selah.

Cease striving - Relax; God has this under control. It is the deterministic chaos, the permitted chaos God understands. He allows all the darkness and sin and evil to work for everyone’s eventual benefit.

Sometimes we cannot diffuse the chaos around us, but we can deflate the chaos within us. How do we do this? Selah! Stop, pause and consider. Count to three. Have a single-minded focus. Chaos cannot compete with single-mindedness!

Let’s finish up the lesson from Philippians 3:

Philippians 3:13-14: 13 Brethren, I do not regard myself as having laid hold of it yet; but one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and reaching forward to what lies ahead, 14 I press on toward the goal for the prize of the upward call of God in Christ Jesus.

This reminds us of the prophecy in Isaiah 50:6-7 which describes Jesus’ trial as a perfect man. It says, I gave my back to those who strike me and my cheeks to those who pluck out the beard and spit on me. But here is his response: For the Lord God helps me...I have set my face like flint. I will not be ashamed.

I have set my face like flint - meaning, he has a stone-cold focus. He will not be moved. He has his objective, and whatever the chaos is that surrounds him, he will follow the leading of his Father.

Chaos: In Habakkuk 3, the prophet prayed about all God had revealed about the coming trouble God’s chosen people were going to experience.

Habakkuk had some fear and ultimately showed great faith:

Habakkuk 3:12-13,16: 12 In indignation You marched through the earth; In anger You trampled the nations. 13 You went forth for the salvation of Your people, for the salvation of Your anointed… 16 I heard and my inward parts trembled, at the sound my lips quivered. Decay enters my bones, and in my place I tremble. Because I must wait quietly for the day of distress, for the people to arise who will invade us.

Habakkuk is saying, I have no choice, and I am trembling inside. My lips are quivering, decay is entering my bones. I am stuck. I don't have a way out. One might look at this and think he’s in rough shape. No, he is just showing us this is how he feels. But this is not who he is because he knows this is permitted chaos, that God has it in hand. Kingdom Attitude in Chaos – the very next verses:

Habakkuk 3:17-19: 17 Though the fig tree should not blossom and there be no fruit on the vines, though the yield of the olive should fail and the fields produce no food, though the flock should be cut off from the fold and there be no cattle in the stalls, 18 Yet I will exult in the LORD, I will rejoice in the God of my salvation. 19 The Lord GOD is my strength, and He has made my feet like hinds' feet, and makes me walk on my high places...

Hind’s feet - mountain goats and rams can scale a cliff with ease. That is the kind of walking Habakkuk feels. He is afraid because of the chaos that is to come and his hands are tied. He can do nothing about it. In the midst of doing nothing about it, what does he do? He diffuses the chaos within by acknowleding that even if the fig tree doesn’t blossom, there is no fruit of the vines and everything fails, he will still rejoice in the Lord God because He knows all and is above all. The vision WILL come. Though it tarries, wait for it; for it will certainly come. In his fear, Habakkuk was determined to have faith in the Lord. His was a prayer of acceptance and maturity.

Chaos Clarifier: God’s hand is ultimately over all and in control. Chaos is a temporary tool He uses to demonstrate our overwhelming need for Him!

The result of God's permitted chaos in His kingdom to come and His will to be done:

Revelation 21:1-4: 1 Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth; for the first heaven and the first earth passed away, and there is no longer any sea (the sea symbolically pictures the restless masses of humanity). 2 And I saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, made ready as a bride adorned for her husband. 3 And I heard a loud voice from the throne, saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is among men, and He will dwell among them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself will be among them, 4 and He will wipe away every tear from their eyes; and there will no longer be any death; there will no longer be any mourning, or crying, or pain; the first things have passed away.

What a powerful assurance of what is going to happen after what is going to happen! We have seen the trouble that is going to happen. It is prophesied; it is sure that it is going to happen. We can be like Habakkuk and say, “Okay, I cannot control it, but I can diffuse the chaos within me so that I can stand for that which is highest and that is God's will and God's way.”

We choose how we stand and what we stand for. We make choices in the midst of chaotic circumstances to either be a light shining for the glory of God, or to be just like everybody else. It's a choice. Find yourself going deeper into the Scriptures to find your strength to be able to be content with the chaos around us, knowing it is God Almighty who controls all.

So, can we be content with chaos?

For Rick, Jonathan and Christian Questions, …think about it!
