1.

Does “chaos” always mean random, unpredictable disorder? Explain. What is “deterministic chaos"? What is “planned chaos”? How does creation illustrate “God’s planned chaos”? (Genesis 1:1-5)

2. How does “God’s permitted chaos” differ from “God’s planned chaos”? Does God use natural disasters and epidemics for His glory? Where is God in the chaos that grips this world, and why can’t we see Him at work? (Habakkuk 1:1-4)

3.

Where does the chaos that affects our lives come from? What are our choices in dealing with it? What was the Apostle Paul’s secret to rejoicing despite chaos and prison in his life? Paul recognized what was behind God’s permitted chaos in his life. What was that? (Philippians 4:10-13)

4. Explain the chaos in each of the following events and the solutions to diffusing the apostle’s reaction to it:

a. The storm on the Sea of Galilee: Mark 4:37-41

b. The arrest of Jesus in the Garden of Gethsemane: Luke 22:47-53, Mark 14:44, Matthew 26:49-56, John 18:4-12

5. How can we diffuse the chaos we intentionally and unintentionally cause?

a. Paul and Barnabas in Iconium: how did they diffuse the chaos they caused?

b. Paul and Barnabas in Lystra: how did human emotions and crowd mentality play into chaos? (Acts 14:11-20) c.

What is an effective technique for dealing with these emotions?

6. Philippians 3:7-8 – What have you counted as loss for the sake of Christ? - (Acts 6:8-15) Stephen’s death illustrated what about chaos? What is a modern example of this? - What questions should we ask ourselves if we are causing or receiving chaos?

7. Philippians 3:9-11 – Are you contributing to the chaos around you? What principles are driving your actions? - How did Jesus contribute to God’s permitted chaos? Why might he have done this? (Matthew 21:12-13)

8. “God’s permitted chaos” brings “God’s perfect kingdom”: In each set of scriptures below, identify the chaos and then the promise of the kingdom.

a. Daniel 12:1 and 2:44 – how do you handle the thought of this chaos? Does Revelation 13:8 help?

b. Psalms 46:1-3, 9-11 – why does this chaos seem familiar today? How do verses 9-11 soothe the chaos in your thoughts? c.

How do the words, Cease striving, Press on, I have set my face like a flint, Selah, give you comfort and guide your reactions? Explain. (Philippians 3:12-14, Isaiah 50:6-7)

9. Was Habakkuk afraid of the chaos God revealed to him in Habakkuk 3:12-16? Describe his reaction. What was his attitude in verses 17-19? How could he react like this?

10. What is the biggest comfort you take away from this episode? If we cannot diffuse the chaos around us, what should we do to conquer our panic? (Revelation 21:1-4)

## Episode 1063 — Is This the Moment You Were Created For? (Part II)
Published: 2019-03-04
Episode page: https://christianquestions.com/character/1063-esther-part-2/

2 Corinthians 5:17: (NASB) Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creature; the old things passed away; behold, new things have come.

Sometimes we are called by destiny. Queen Esther of the Old Testament showed us what can happen when circumstances open the door for uncharacteristic heroism. Several weeks ago, we told the story of how a Jewish teenage girl kept her calm and found a way to save her people at great personal risk. She worked within the constraints of her ancient society to rise to the highest level attainable, all while remaining focused and humble. Her story has inspired people for centuries and left scholars to dissect its literary construction and contemporary significance. As with much of the Bible, there are layers of lessons to explore, and Esther is no exception! Esther’s story can be seen to parallel the walk of a Christian in thought-provoking and unique ways. What do Esther’s experiences teach us about our faith and our choices?

This podcast is largely based on the work of a Bible scholar named Carl Hagensick. His insights have opened the door for us to analyze the book of Esther on a much deeper level by overlaying the path of our individual Christian walk onto the story. We recommend first listening to Part 1 of this podcast, Episode #1057, where we walked through the book of Esther in its entirety to find many modern life lessons.

Picture the story of Esther as a stage play on two stages taking place simultaneously. For the first stage, we want to introduce you to the cast of characters involved.

Playing simultaneously on the other stage, there is only one actor: YOU, your Christian life. We will divide YOU into various roles as well, so this will be Your Personal Stage.

2 Corinthians 5:17: (NASB) Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creature; the old things passed away; behold, new things have come.

Those called to follow Christ, who surrender their own wills to do the will of God with the help of God’s Holy Spirit (His power and influence) are called NEW CREATURES. This is our new spiritual life.

Who is going to control Ahasuerus…Haman or Mordecai? Who is going to be the counselor who carries the weight in the kingdom? Haman operating directly, or Mordecai operating through Esther/Esther operating through Mordecai?

The same plot applies on the second stage, Your Personal Stage.

Who is going to control YOUR MIND? Is it going to be the FLESH (Haman) or the HOLY SPIRIT (Mordecai) working through the NEW CREATURE (Esther)?

Any good drama is divided into acts and scenes, and the book of Esther is no exception. We will look at the purpose of 12 scenes on these two stages – the Story Stage and Your Personal Stage.

Our Old Testament hero, Esther, will feed our New Testament discipleship! How will that work?

As with any Bible related experience, we draw lessons and principles by understanding the thinking, intentions and actions of those we observe. It is paramount that we remember Esther and Mordecai were always about faithfulness to God, Haman was always about himself and King Ahasuerus was the key decision maker. Who will influence the king?

Ahasuerus had a great banquet for the representatives of all the provinces in the City of Sushan at the palace. During the banquet he commanded his wife, Queen Vashti, to come and present herself at the banquet. Vashti refused, and as a result was divorced by the king. Why did Vashti refuse? The Bible does not specifically say, but this scene shows us the more central issue – think of this scene as the role of man and woman in the marriage relationship. Scene 1 was definitely not written by the women of the #metoo movement! We have to remember the strict patriarchal society of the time.

The reason for the drama in this first scene:

Esther 1:16-20: (NASB) 16 In the presence of the king and the princes, Memucan (Memucan was a prince and one of the king’s counsellors) said, Queen Vashti has wronged not only the king but also all the princes and all the peoples who are in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus. (He reigned over 127 provinces including modern-day Turkey, Iraq, Iran, Pakistan, Jordan, Lebanon, Israel and parts of other countries) 17 For the queen’s conduct will become known to all the women causing them to look with contempt on their husbands by saying, King Ahasuerus commanded Queen Vashti to be brought in to his presence, but she did not come. 18 This day the ladies of Persia and Media who have heard of the queen’s conduct will speak in the same way to all the king’s princes, and there will be plenty of contempt and anger. 19 If it pleases the king, let a royal edict be issued by him and let it be written in the laws of Persia and Media so that it cannot be repealed, that Vashti may no longer come into the presence of King Ahasuerus, and let the king give her royal position to another who is more worthy than she. 20 When the king’s edict which he will make is heard throughout all his kingdom, great as it is, then all women will give honor to their husbands, great and small.

This was the core of the issue. In the society of that day, the woman was to be directed by the husband. He was, in the fullest sense, the “head of the house.” She was, in the fullest sense, part of the “body.” He was the head, and she was to do his wishes.

Vashti violated the custom of the day. If she had been allowed to get away with it, as the queen of the whole realm, this would pass down to all the wives and be a general women’s rights movement that they feared would spread at least to the degree of the rule of the household of man and wife. For this reason, the king listened to the advice of Memucan recommending that Vashti

be banished and replaced by a new queen. How does this translate into the drama of scene 1 on Your Personal Stage?

Before we were called to God we had many “feast days” in our lives, happy celebrations and great events. But always there was one thing that spoiled our happiness. Whenever our MIND would tell our body to do something right, something righteous, the FLESH had its own way. The body said, “I don’t really want to,” and it would reject the commandments of the MIND. We found that the good we would do, we could not do. The OLD CREATURE would not be confined to the nobler, higher elements the MIND would require. This was insurrection of the very worst kind.

As a result, we finally came to a place where we recognized the counsel and calling from God. We realized if we permit this insurrection to continue, our whole life would be in turmoil and simply run an unfulfilled natural course. We came to the place where we recognized I must find a better self than the self I am. “Getting rid of Vashti” is the coming to the place where we divorce ourselves from the OLD CREATURE and begin looking for a new life.

The Apostle Paul gave us an insight into this internal battle:

Romans 7:14-25: (NASB) 14For we know that the Law is spiritual, but I am of flesh, sold into bondage to sin. 15For what I am doing, I do not understand; for I am not practicing what I would like to do, but I am doing the very thing I hate. 16 But if I do the very thing I do not want to do, I agree with the Law, confessing that the Law is good. 17So now, no longer am I the one doing it, but sin which dwells in me. 18 For I know that nothing good dwells in me, that is, in my flesh; for the willing is present in me, but the doing of the good is not. 19For the good that I want, I do not do, but I practice the very evil that I do not want. 20But if I am doing the very thing I do not want, I am no longer the one doing it, but sin which dwells in me. 21 I find then the principle that evil is present in me, the one who wants to do good. 22For I joyfully concur with the law of God in the inner man, 23 but I see a different law in the members of my body, waging war against the law of my mind and making me a prisoner of the law of sin which is in my members. 24Wretched man that I am! Who will set me free from the body of this death? 25Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, on the one hand I myself with my mind am serving the law of God, but on the other, with my flesh the law of sin.

The world has a lot to offer, and we can become ensnared by it.

The king decided to get rid of Vashti as his queen but did not know who to put in her place. He had no one in mind; he had not planned before that day to get rid of her until this event took place. He holds a “Miss Medo-Persia” contest with all the young women of the realm. They would all be brought before the king, and he would choose his new wife.

One of the king’s counselors, Mordecai, a foreigner, a Jew, sends his cousin named Hadassah into this “contest.” She is an orphan, and he is her guardian. Even though the girls probably did not have a say in the matter, we can assume this was important to them, as it was a great honor to be married to the king. Josephus the historian wrote that there were about 400 candidates.

The king made arrangements for all of the girls to appear at their very best. He had the keeper of his harem give them whatever they would require – any cosmetic, robe, garment, jewelry - anything that would make them the most beautiful to win the approval of the king.

Finally, the turn came for Hadassah to go in and present herself before the king:

Esther 2:12-13,15: (NASB) 12Now when the turn of each young lady came to go in to King Ahasuerus, after the end of her twelve months under the regulations for the women—for the days of their beautification were completed as follows: six months with oil of myrrh and six months with spices and the cosmetics for women - 13the young lady would go in to the king in this way: anything that she desired was given her to take with her from the harem to the king’s palace. … 15Now when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai who had taken her as his daughter, came to go in to the king, she did not request anything except what Hegai, the king’s eunuch who was in charge of the women, advised. And Esther found favor in the eyes of all who saw her.

She was the only one who said, “No makeup or jewelry, please. I will go in just as I am.” She was the only one who appeared the fairest of all the women. Her name was changed from Hadassah, which means “myrtle tree,” a symbol of bitterness and sorrow, to Esther, meaning “star.” As a result, she wins the contest, becomes the queen and is crowned as the one to replace Vashti.

When we come to that place in our MIND where we decide that the OLD CREATURE is not righteous, we decide we want a new life, a new passion. We look around at our prospects: there is business, education, social work, philosophy, being a person who lives life for whatever pleasure or fulfillment life will bring. But for all the things we look at, there is one higher element introduced to us - following Christ as a NEW CREATURE by a higher influence, the HOLY SPIRIT. This higher prospect for life stands alone, because it is entirely different!

As we look at all the other prospects in our lives, we “dress them up” in their very best. When we look at the prospect of education, we think of ourselves as excelling. If we look at ourselves in medicine, we think of ourselves as becoming a great surgeon, maybe discovering the cure for a disease. We put all the “cosmetics” we can on each thing we look at.

But when the HOLY SPIRIT presents to us the concept of the NEW CREATURE in Christ, it tells it like it is. There are no cosmetics or fancy expensive clothes. It is presented plainly as genuine, for what it is – a way of sacrifice that, if followed, is able to produce Christlikeness. Of all the things we have looked at, this is the most beautiful. This is what I want for my life!

Just as the girls had an unlimited amount of choices in clothing and jewels, we also have unlimited opportunities to spend our time. But the Christian is called to a life of sacrifice to move higher.

We come to that place where instead of being a myrtle (bitter), we repent and come into a spiritual realm where we are Esther (a star), something that belongs to God and away from earthly things.

Esther 3:1: (NASB) After these events King Ahasuerus promoted Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him and established his authority over all the princes who were with him.

Haman becomes the chief counselor of the king. Haman loves his new high position as Number 2 right under the king. He required that all men show their recognition and respect of his high position by bowing down to him. Everybody bows, but one:

Esther 3:2: (NASB) All the king’s servants who were at the king’s gate bowed down and paid homage to Haman; for so the king had commanded concerning him. But Mordecai neither bowed down nor paid homage.

Mordecai would not compromise his principles even if there were consequences.

As a result, Haman became extremely angry at Mordecai and said, “I’m going to take it out on that man and everyone like him. He represents the most stubborn, hard-headed person around; he must be a Jew. So, let’s get rid of him, and let’s get rid of all those people.” Haman makes plans and casts lots (the Persian word for “lots” was “purim”) that on a certain day he will get rid of all of Mordecai’s people, after seeking the king’s permission.

Right after he gets power, Haman makes plans to eliminate whoever would stand in the way of that power.

It is interesting that this Haman was an Agagite. An Agagite means a person who comes from Agag.

We went into a lot of detail in Part 1 about what being an Agagite meant, and it is fascinating.

We backtrack roughly 1,000 years to see how we got to this point. Haman was a direct descendent of Amalek, the grandson of Jacob’s brother, Esau. Amalek became a tribe, and the Amalekites were known for their love of self and reliance on violence to prove their superiority. They insisted God was absent in the world, and everything happened by chance. This is contrary to what the Jews believe and what the book of Esther teaches. Agag was an Amalekite king.

We read about Agag in 1 Samuel 15 when Saul was king of Israel, and he was VERY SPECIFICALLY told to slay all of the Amalekites, and even all their animals, and not to spare one of them. In a triumphant procession, Saul comes back into the city and the prophet of the Lord, Samuel, said, “What’s the sound of cattle I hear? I thought you were going to kill all the cattle?” Saul said, “Who wants to do that? This makes a nice bounty of war. We are going to sacrifice these to God in due time.” Samuel asked, “Who are these slaves I am seeing walking by? Those are Amalekites!” Saul responds, “Well, these are the very best and noblest. We can use them – right here we have the king, Agag!” Capturing the king alive would have played to Saul’s ego.

If you never had Agag, you would never have had an Agagite. As a result, Samuel kills the king.

Samuel kills Agag the next day, but either the night Agag was allowed to live, or before he was captured, he had relations with his wife and she conceived, or perhaps the sons of Agag were permitted to escape to Egypt. Either way, if Saul had been faithful 1,000 years prior, the book of Esther would never have the plot that developed. There would not be an Agagite in our story with his generational hatred of the Jews. COMPLETE OBEDIENCE TO GOD SAVES LATER REGRET.

Soon after we give our lives to God, we are faced with an ugly truth: our human desires are NOT dead. We got rid of the OLD CREATURE, but our FLESHLY desires grab hold of our affections and tell us internally, “Now, I do not really mind that you are a Christian, as long as you pay due homage to me, as long as you give me sufficient vacation time, luxuries of life, make sure I have a nice house to live in and a nice car to drive and you reverence me, that will be fine. You just go ahead and be a Christian.” And everyone bows down to this except GOD’S SPIRIT – His power and influence in our lives. GOD’S SPIRIT says, “That is not the way you were called to! You said you were willing to give these things up, and until you are willing to do so, you will not be truly walking in Jesus’ footsteps.”

Faced with this dilemma we answer back to God, “Your way is so different from mine. I can’t live this kind of life. I have to have these things,” and we begin to develop thoughts and feelings within the flesh and try to push the NEW CREATURE out. This can be subtle – it can begin with little sins, little things that come in that we did not quite get rid of when we committed to walk in Jesus’ footsteps.

These are our “Agagites” that tell us WE have a better way, not God. If we had really been faithful at the very beginning and “killed Agag,” these things would not be coming up. But because we left a few Agagites to escape, they come back to haunt us and begin pressing for honor in our lives.

For more on dealing with temptations, please search our archives for Episode #986: “How Do I Deal With Enticing Temptations?”

It contains specific steps to overcome temptation using the advice from James 4:7-10.

We need to identify our Agagites. Where are our weak areas? Bring them out into the light and look at how ugly they are. There are a lot of ways we can cover them up and justify them.

When things are enticing, we need to apply the “letter of the law” and not the “spirit of the law.” Err on the side of caution even if we are being TOO cautious.

There is an internal struggle in our MINDS reflected in the story of Esther. The FLESH begins to deviously plot how it can rid itself of these higher spiritual desires.

How does Queen Esther show us the way to defeat our greatest enemy, which happens to be ourselves?

We do plot and scheme against God’s influence in our lives, and it is SO easy to justify those schemes. After all, we are still very human, and we do have wants, needs and desires that rightfully belong to us. This is where the battle in each of our minds can easily and carelessly commit us to directions and decisions that are NOT in our best interest.

Haman’s desire is to rid the empire of all of the Jewish people because of his anger against Mordecai. But he does not have the power to do it, because only Ahasuerus can sign the decree.

Haman approaches Ahasuerus with his proposition and uses two lines of reasoning to convince Ahasuerus that this should be done:

Esther 3:8-9: (NASB) 8Then Haman said to King Ahasuerus, There is a certain people scattered and dispersed among the peoples in all the provinces of your kingdom; their laws are different from those of all other people and they do not observe the king’s laws, so it is not in the king’s interest to let them remain.9 If it is pleasing to the king, let it be decreed that they be destroyed, and I will pay ten thousand talents of silver into the hands of those who carry on the king’s business, to put into the king’s treasuries.

This looks like it was a two-pronged attack.

“Ahasuerus, if you are going to have a unified kingdom, you have to have the same laws for all people. There are a certain people in the land, (he did not reveal that he meant the Jewish people) that have a different God, different laws, and it just doesn’t work to have such a diverse culture among your people. You cannot allow this to continue. Rid yourself of this! And besides, if that’s not enough for you, here is a bribe: 10,000 pieces of silver for your treasury.”

Presumably this money would have come from the murdered Jewish people. A little bribery never hurt, right?

Ahasuerus says, “That’s not a bad idea; I’ll go along with that,” and he signs the decree to get rid of all the Jews not realizing Haman’s secondary agenda.

As the FLESH begins its counterattack against our design to be a SPIRIT-DRIVEN follower of Jesus, it presents two arguments to the mind: “You know, you are a hypocrite! Every time you try to be a Christian, you are doing what is not natural to you. Your heart really isn’t in it! The law of the SPIRIT is different from the law of the FLESH. Face it – you are earthly; you can’t really live a spiritual life, and as a result, it is not in your best interest to keep this constant battle going in your mind. It is better you forget about all that spiritual stuff. It is too diverse from what you are. And besides, if you do that, I’ve got a little present for you. I will get you involved in business - you can make a fortune! Let’s get you to have the home you want, drive the kind of car you want. You know you can! Focusing on material things is so much more sensible and natural.”

Now your MIND acquiesces to your FLESHLY desires: “I guess that’s probably right,” you say, “I’m not really qualified to run this race; it is too big for me anyway.” This is discouragement. In our Christian life, we “sign the decree” and say, “I will drop spiritual things for a while.”

We say, “I am not good enough, so the Lord is not calling me.”

The FLESH starts playing on our MIND – “What is the point? There are so many other things you can do and be.” We need to fight against discouragement.

For help with discouragement and feeling overwhelmed, please search our archives for Episode #924: “How Do You Stand When Life Gets Too Heavy?”

When someone comes to me and says, “I am not good enough,” my immediate response is, “You know what? You aren’t. And neither am I.” This is a walk of grace. Whenever we get discouraged, we inevitably forget grace. Hebrews 4:16: (KJV) Let us come boldly unto the throne of grace. It is not the “throne of measurement” or the “throne of accomplishment.”

It is the throne of grace. The grace of God through Christ helps us to get up again. It is okay to fall down. Get back up and ask for God’s grace. We are not good enough, but Jesus is. Jesus is covering us and representing us as our Advocate to the Lord. It is his goodness we are using in order to fight our way back to God.

Fortunately, this is not the end and there is a hero in this story.

Esther is in the palace, totally oblivious to what is happening. She does not even notice that there has been a decree against the Jewish people. She has gotten into the routine of daily royal living. But Mordecai puts on sackcloth and ashes and sits right in front of her window, wailing. She says, “It is not appropriate for my cousin to be carrying on in such a way when I’m queen of the realm. He should be happy!”

She sends new clothes for him to put on, but he refuses to change clothes and begins his argument:

Esther 4:13,14: (NASB) 13 Then Mordecai told them to reply to Esther, Do not imagine that you in the king’s palace can escape any more than all the Jews. 14 For if you remain silent at this time, relief and deliverance will arise for the Jews from another place and you and your father’s house will perish. And who knows whether you have not attained royalty for such a time as this? Never underestimate the power of a voice with influence. Mordecai commanded respect!

Haman was not the only one with a two-pronged argument. Mordecai says to Esther, “Our God is not weak. He will deliver the Jews, with or without our help.” It is not dependent upon Esther. But if she does not help, her life is at stake. She will not be delivered, because she and her father’s house will be cut off. “And besides,” he questions, “why do you think you became queen in the first place? Maybe that is the very reason the Lord has put you in this position, so you can fight this battle and win this victory for God’s people.” And Esther says, “I’ll think about it.” Fear for one’s life is a BIG obstacle. She takes three days to fast and pray and think it over.

This is the true effect of her respect for Mordecai – deep and soul-searching consideration:

Esther 4:16: (NASB) Go, assemble all the Jews who are found in Susa, and fast for me; do not eat or drink for three days, night or day. I and my maidens also will fast in the same way. And thus I will go in to the king, which is not according to the law; and if I perish, I perish. She recognized that one did not come to the king without his bidding. She said, “It’s been 30 days since I’ve seen the king.” This is an important element we will talk about soon.

When we come to those places of discouragement, we go on blissfully unaware for a while. We say, “I’ll get by.” Every day can’t be euphoric. We live in the world, and we have to put up with the world! In short, we get comfortable and settle. It takes God’s HOLY SPIRIT, His power and influence, to show us how desperate we really are.

The HOLY SPIRIT presents us with two arguments: “God has a plan, and in that plan He calls a select few to follow in Jesus’ footsteps – to live and die for the will of God. Through these called-out disciples comes the deliverance for the whole world of mankind. This will happen – with or without YOU. If you do not wake up, your spiritual opportunity will cease because you hesitated. It is not dependent upon you, but YOU are dependent upon you. And besides, maybe the Lord called you because He wanted you to fight this special battle, so you would save others and have a special place in that kingdom, because you had overcome in this particular area in your life.”

God’s direction helps us overcome the lethargy of the FLESH. When the HOLY SPIRIT shows us something so significant, the “ESTHER” in us – our NEW CREATURE listens! It presses itself into the action of seeking and following a directive from God. We pray and consider deeply.

This response begins the phase of recovery in the book of Esther and in our lives.

After not communicating with the king for 30 days, Esther could not have predicted what the king’s mood was after their last meeting. She was really taking a chance.

In our Christian walk, we may come to a time when we have been distracted and have temporarily lost touch with our “true north.” This time away from spiritual things brings us to a point of discouragement. Finally we realize, “I’ve got to make a stand for the Lord. I can’t let it go. If I perish, I perish.” We decide we HAVE to make a stand for God and assert our true calling of discipleship.

Once we have been away from the Lord for a period of time, we start doubting if God will bring us back in. It is the lesson of the Prodigal Son. Have I gone so far that I am not worth recovering?

We need to trust our “Mordecai,” the HOLY SPIRIT, God’s power and influence, within us. As the saying goes, Esther did not know what the future held, but she knew who held the future. Because of the trust she had in Mordecai, she was able to act.

We do not get to see what is right in front of us, but we know that with God’s power and influence, we have the ability to move forward.

When she first approached the king, she had no makeup or fancy clothes and just went as she was. That now changes:

Esther 5:1-3: (NASB) 1Now it came about on the third day that Esther put on her royal robes and stood in the inner court of the king’s palace in front of the king’s rooms, and the king was sitting on his royal throne in the throne room, opposite the entrance to the palace. 2When the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, she obtained favor in his sight; and the king extended to Esther the golden scepter which was in his hand. So Esther came near and touched the top of the scepter. 3Then the king said to her, What is troubling you, Queen Esther? And what is your request? Even to half of the kingdom it shall be given to you.

Can you picture the scene? She is so apprehensive. This time she dresses up and puts on her very best clothes – the garments of royalty - and hangs out by the door. He sees her and says, “Where have you been? I haven’t seen you in a month! What do you want? You can have anything up to half the kingdom!”

When that NEW CREATURE – that spirit begotten mind - says, “I am going to claim my royal standing and my justification. I will put on the royal robes and say, ‘Lord, you called me, you keep me!’” It then begins to present itself again, standing humbly yet royally. The NEW CREATURE is royalty because it is of God.

As soon as our MIND sees this, it thinks, “Where have you been? I have not thought about you for so long. I LOVE spiritual things! Anything you want – half the kingdom – it is yours! What do you want?”

Esther said, “What I really want is to invite you to dinner. Bring Haman with you – let’s have a banquet.” This must have puzzled the king. She did not ask for anything – she just wanted to have dinner.

Our spiritual mind, our NEW CREATURE, says the same thing. It really wants the clear and personal attention of our physical mind.

Now that our attention is focused, what has to be done for the mind of Christ to win the day?

When God’s power is at work in our spiritual mind, it is never hurried or rash. God called us for a reason and when we do falter, He has a way of showing us not only where we went wrong but what to do about it as well. Queen Esther clearly illustrates this spiritual thinking as she turns the tables.

She prepared a royal feast with wine and food. She laid out the fruits, and the kings says, “This is delightful. I am sure you want something from me, though. What do you want? It is yours up to half the kingdom.” She intriguingly says, “I do have a favor to ask: I would like you to come back to another dinner.”

When our NEW CREATURE, our spiritual mind, begins asserting itself, and the MIND asks, “What do you want?” the NEW CREATURE answers, “I want to show you something. I want to show you the prospects I showed you way back when. I want to lay out in front of you the bounty of the fruit of the Spirit: patience, joy, longsuffering, etc. I want you to taste those fruits.” When the MIND begins tasting them, it thinks, “Delicious! What do you want?” “I want you to come taste them again.” The NEW CREATURE holds back. The time is not quite right to reveal its full scope of truth, because something has not yet happened. We will find out what that is as we go forward in our drama.

No wonder he could not sleep – he is so curious to know what the queen wanted. She was smart and unpredictable, and that made her more desirable. With insomnia, it sometimes helps to find the most boring thing you can find and try to read it so it puts you to sleep. So he said, “Read me the history books! Get the king’s chronicles out.” As they were reading to him, they read about a time when there was a plot against his life that Mordecai had uncovered. “I forgot all about that. What did we do for Mordecai?” “We didn’t do a thing.” “Tomorrow morning, we are going to correct THAT.”

This is the real turning point in our Christian lives. When the NEW CREATURE, our spiritual mind, reasserts its ascendency over our physical MIND, we might literally spend some sleepless nights. We toss, we turn, we wonder, we think, we ask…what is expected of me? We begin reviewing our life and remember back when we first heard the call of God. We remember how things were in our way that could have destroyed us, because Satan does not want us to

follow God. There was a plot to kill us – just as Satan put death before all of mankind. We remember God’s providence. Our human MIND thinks, “What did I ever do to express gratitude for that spiritual influence? Nothing. Tomorrow morning, I’m going to fix that.” And with that, we rest.

This is the time we really embrace Christian growth in our MIND. The battle shifts, and we are becoming more spiritual. But the next morning, something happens.

The king wakes up refreshed and says, “The first order of business, we have to do something for Mordecai, but what? If I only had a good counselor to talk to.” Haman had just come in for approval to have Mordecai personally killed, so he was in the king’s court. “Bring Haman in! Haman, I have a problem. There is someone in this kingdom I want to honor, and I don’t know how to do that properly. What would you suggest?”

Haman said, “Oh! I know what you have in mind.” If he were humble, Haman would have asked who the king was talking about. Pride is blinding. Haman says, “I will tell you what – put this man on your own horse. Put a crown on the horse so everyone knows it is the king’s horse, give him your best robe, take your most trusted servant, and lead him through the streets of the city and say, “Hey everybody, this is a man the king likes! This is the one of favor; the king is honoring this man!”

And the king says, “Great idea! You be the servant; do that to Mordecai!”

Haman had to do it. Now he was really mad: “I got the order to kill the Jews, but I am still not happy as long as Mordecai is alive.”

When we wake up that next morning, we ask ourselves, “What would I do if I wanted to be honored?” We want to tell how good we are, especially now that we are on the right path. We want others to know we have something to offer. So, we suggest this to our human MIND. “If I really wanted to honor myself, I would let others know what a good person I am.” But now, our MIND as a NEW CREATURE announces, “That’s exactly what I want you to do. You tell everybody how good God’s HOLY SPIRIT is. You tell everybody what His providence has done for you.”

“Wait! That wasn’t the plan! It was about ME, how good I am, not about how good God’s power is!” When we obey our NEW CREATURE, our FLESH must obey. The flesh is irritated and might even get annoyed, but spirituality reigns now and that means the exultation of God’s power - His HOLY SPIRIT! People ask how, 21 years later, we can produce a podcast every week. This opportunity to talk about God’s word to people all over the world is overwhelming in its privilege and in its responsibilities. I manage it by looking at just one week at a time and by the grace of God. This is what helps me cope. I ask, “What am I supposed to do this week, and how does the grace of God deliver me to be able to get it done?” God does not open doors and just make it easy. Sometimes the opportunity goes through tunnels and over mountains. Looking at the big picture is too scary, because it is a never-ending thing. “Just for this week, Lord, how can I rely on your grace to get my responsibilities accomplished?” This is what gets me through. I have to keep God’s grace and His Spirit up front.

A second banquet was held. The king asked, “Esther, I know you want something besides continuing to invite me to supper. What is it?” Esther responded, “I do have a problem. There is somebody who is trying to kill me.” “But you’re the queen!” “Someone wants to kill me and my people as well.” “Who is that wicked person?” She points, “Haman there!” Haman freaked out, and this was the last thing he or the king expected. The king goes outside to cool off. Haman throws himself at the queen and says, “Mercy!” The king comes in at this exact moment, and the optics are bad.

The king roars, “And now you are attacking the queen as well? Right in front of me?” The king interprets this wrong and calls for his guards to hang Haman. His anger knows no bounds. Haman’s death sentence is given in this chapter.

The first banquet is when the NEW CREATURE begins first asserting itself. It set before us the fruit of the Spirit. The second banquet is when it begins showing us we can make progress, that we can attain this fruit of the Spirit. This shows growth and maturity. It shows us now we have the wine (a symbol of joy) besides the fruit. We begin processing the reality of this powerful spiritual prospect.

The king is our MIND. Haman is our OLD CREATURE doing what we know is not right. It is not enough to love righteousness, but according to Hebrews 1:9 as quoted from Psalm 45:7, we are supposed to hate evil. When our MIND is looking at the two of them, our FLESH (Haman) vs. NEW CREATURE (Esther), we have to get rid of that FLESH.

That is when we know whatever the NEW CREATURE wants, “she” can have. We can obtain the joys of the Lord set before us. And we ask, “What are those? What do you want?” All we really want is to live. The FLESH wants to take the life of the NEW CREATURE by distraction, disappointment and failure. Just like the king, we go out and think it over, for it is a concept that is hard to grasp. Now the FLESH, like Haman, begins begging for itself. The MIND says, “That’s IT! The FLESH is always taking advantage of the NEW CREATURE, the spiritual mind. I am going to be rid of this FLESH once and for all.” We come to that determination, and we completely put down the FLESH in our lives.

It is interesting that when this happens, something else happens:

Esther 8:1-2: (NASB) 1On that day King Ahasuerus gave the house of Haman, the enemy of the Jews, to Queen Esther; and Mordecai came before the king, for Esther had disclosed what he was to her. 2The king took off his signet ring which he had taken away from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai. And Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.

This is one of the most profound passages in the entire book. It reveals to us the place in our lives where we no longer just think about and promise to give up the FLESH, but we actually give it up! Once the FLESH is destroyed we are truly given control over the stewardship of all that the FLESH had previously owned. Now we are in harmony – the HOLY SPIRIT drives our spiritual mind, our NEW CREATURE, and our humanity - both MIND and body - dutifully follow.

The victory is won although there are still a few scenes left in our drama. With Haman gone, how does the king undo the evil of a proclaimed edict that cannot be undone?

The story of Esther gives a true sense of reality. If this were a fictional movie script, the removing of Haman, his diabolical plots and the elevation of Mordecai would have served as a perfect ending. However, life does not work that way. There is always more to fight, more to do and others to save.

The law of the Medes and Persians was a special law that could not be broken. The king himself could not remand the law. Without realizing his beloved Esther was Jewish, he had commanded that all the Jews be attacked and killed, and he could not change it, despite that he saw the law was wrong. He said, “I will make another law, where the Jews can defend themselves.” This would discourage those who would kill a Jew, as they were not counting on them having weapons to fight back. Despite that second decree, people still tried but were slaughtered because God blessed the Jews. There were so many slaughtered but not enough to get rid of all their enemies - that they had another war for a second day.

We still have battles to fight!

There are two edicts. We cannot change the original edict – we cannot change our past, but we can adjust the trajectory of what is going to happen in spite of it. The second edict says, “Fight back from what your past has done so you can stand before God.”

God’s providence extends differently in this scene. He did not give the FLESH (Haman) victory over the SPIRIT (Mordecai), but He also is not going to give your NEW CREATURE (Esther) the victory over the extended FLESHLY desires of Haman’s unjust decree upon all faithful ones. What God does provide is the weapons with which to fight this evil. Victory takes work.

God tells us that the battle is ours, and if we fight in His SPIRIT we will win, no question about it. This causes many elements of the FLESH to say, “I do not want to fight someone who is going to fight back!” Other elements of the FLESH are more stubborn and still want to fight.

We do not just sit back as Christians and wait for God to take care of us. We still have to fight because we are still living IN the world; the goal is to not live OF the world. Our previous decisions in life may have set us on a path that needs correcting. God says, “Work on it. Fight the darkness from your experiences.”

If we keep our trust in those weapons, we will find they are mighty through God in the pulling down of strongholds. (2 Corinthians 10:4) Those weapons counter the enemies of the HOLY SPIRIT and of the NEW CREATURE, and the enemies are, one by one, defeated in the lives of the faithful.

In the story of Esther, there was an unexpected side effect of this battle. While many of the enemies of the Jews were slaughtered, something else happened:

Esther 8:17: (NASB) In each and every province and in each and every city, wherever the king’s commandment and his decree arrived, there was gladness and joy for the Jews, a feast and a holiday. And many among the peoples of the land became Jews, for the dread of the Jews had fallen on them.

All of a sudden, some of the people thought it was not a bad idea to convert to Judaism! They could not deny God’s providence and power. People notice.

That is just as important on our personal stage:

Matthew 5:16: (KJV) Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.

Everybody does not glorify God now just because they see our good works. They may hate us. But it glorifies God, and inevitably in God’s future kingdom they will see it.

All the witnessing we do and all the words we preach are good and necessary, but must be backed up by true sacrificial Christian living. This is a spiritual victory that is seen and felt by those we touch. The greater battle for the people comes later in God’s plan, and the outward evidence of God’s light putting down its enemies of darkness for all to see is what will eventually win that day. When the people see the power of His providence and His will, many in the land will begin to turn from their sins.

We can do this on a smaller level now in our lives, but it will happen on a larger scale according to God’s prophecies.

Preach the gospel. Use words if necessary. – Rick’s Uncle Steve

It was a great day for the Jews. They had a feast of joy and gladness, and they decided to have this feast to commemorate this event every year. The feast of Purim is a time of rejoicing and happiness, commemorating the day when God, through Esther, saved their people. This year Purim will be celebrated on March 20 and 21, 2019. And so, if God’s HOLY SPIRIT through our new MIND is gaining control of our FLESH, the story is not over unless we have our feast of Purim. This feast is like having Ebenezers, the things we do to commemorate, to remember, those victories the Lord has given us. Samuel set a stone of remembrance called an Ebenezer to commemorate God’s help to the Israelites in their victory over the Philistines. In 1 Samuel 7:12, he said, Hitherto has the Lord helped us. It is good for us to set up our Ebenezers so we can recall all the times the Lord helped us.

It might be verbally counting our blessings, a song we sing over and over again; it might be the verse of a Psalm we memorized at the time of that trial; it might be sharing that experience with those in our congregation, where we say, Hitherto has the Lord helped us.

It is here that our personal story can find a conclusion. Only after such trauma and faithfulness are we then able to celebrate the victories that our “Mordecai” has taught our “Esther” to give us in our lives. These show us how our NEW CREATURE controls the MIND and how the HOLY SPIRIT does become our chief counselor. It is a victory won by never giving up on the grace of God and His power and influence in our lives.

A friend of mine asked me to respond to the rhetorical question, Is anything too hard for the Lord? asked in Genesis 18:14 and Jeremiah 32:27. Of course the answer is no, but because we have free will with its ability to choose, It can be difficult for the Lord to change our stubborn, selfish ways. It may be difficult for God to change our hearts (not counting some supernatural intervention). Even after seeing all of His goodness and knowing that righteousness trumps sin every time, we fall into temptation, we doubt, we second guess and we fall into a routine without moving forward with purpose and intention to bring Him glory. Who will control our MIND? Our spiritual mind, our NEW CREATURE, must have such influence over our physical MIND that we will bring glory to God.

This account is an interesting introduction to what would happen a generation later. The book of Nehemiah recounts the events of the Jews finally being permitted to go back to Israel and rebuild the city walls of Jerusalem. In Nehemiah 2, when Nehemiah sought this decree, the king and queen gave the decree to go back and rebuild the walls. Esther set a precedent for the Jews to be able to take care of themselves. It is reasonable to assume that her influence was still there as a major backdrop to Nehemiah’s work.

Our lives can have an influence on others.

This has been a great example how no matter how many times you look at the Bible, there is always a new gem to uncover. God has allowed us to have this book of Esther to reveal so many lessons, reminders and warnings for our own Christian walk.

This is a story of victory and heroism in the Old Testament, but it is also a story of victory and heroism in our own life. Focus on the details of our own mind and the battle that goes on within us. God’s power and influence should be our counselor, guiding us and giving our new mind the strength to overcome and live a life that is a glory to Him.

So, is this the moment you were created for?

For Jonathan and Rick (and Julie!) and Christian Questions...

## Episode 1236 — Can Christianity and Paganism Work Together? (Part II)
Published: 2022-07-04
Episode page: https://christianquestions.com/doctrine/1236-wicca/

Exodus 20:1,3: (NASB) 1Then God spoke all these words, saying 3You shall have no other gods before Me.

Last week we examined modern day Paganism and compared it with some of the most basic tenants of Christianity as revealed in the Bible. What we found were two fundamentally different approaches to life in the areas of worship and morality. We can see that as Christians, we are to absolutely love those who hold such a contrary belief system to ours, but that does not mean we support the standards they choose to live by. Now, what about Wicca, which is “white” witchcraft and built on the basis of Pagan beliefs? As Christians, we might simply say that our answer here should be obvious. However, there are claims that the Bible is only condemnatory of “black” magic and “black” witchcraft and that Wicca is not included in those verses. Could this be true? What does the Bible really teach on these matters?

Our conversation will center on Wicca and witchcraft. The objective is NOT to tear down anyone who shares Wiccan or witchcraft beliefs, but it is to be truthful about the differences those beliefs have with true Christianity. We stand for being loving and kind to every single human being, as that is the example that Jesus, our Lord and Savior, left for us to follow.

Paganism, witchcraft and Wicca are three separate terms but with much overlap because their definitions are so broad.

- In Part I we talked extensively about Paganism and how it varies greatly between practitioners. In general, it is an earth-based faith, worshipping nature and its cycles. It can also be polytheistic, worshipping many gods, or some consider everything and everyone to be divine.
- Traditional witchcraft is generally defined as the practice of magic, especially for evil purposes, and the use of spells. In a modern context, it is a religious practice involving magic and an affinity with nature, usually within a Pagan tradition.
- Wicca is often called “white” witchcraft, or witchcraft for a beneficial or positive purpose. It is the best-known form of modern Paganism and is often “ditheistic” involving the supernatural powers of two deities – a god and a goddess. Can you be a Christian and a Wiccan? It depends on whose word you are willing to accept! Yes, you can, Can You Be a Christian and a Witch, Owlvine Green - So, I want to talk about something today that has been coming up a lot lately. I've been getting heaps of questions about, and this is something that I have seen since I began practicing, but particularly lately. And that is, can I be a Christian and a witch? Can I be a Christian and explore other faiths? Can I be a Christian and do magic? Yes, you absolutely can. That is the long and short

of it. There are plenty of people out there who will say no, and honestly, I think a lot of that has to do with their own personal experience and hurts and issues that they have around Christianity.

Before we begin to respond to this, let’s get a better sense of what Wicca is. (Source: https://www.wicca.com/wicca/what-is-wicca.html - What Wicca Is) Witchcraft is a spiritual system that fosters the free thought and will of the individual, encourages learning and an understanding of the earth and nature thereby affirming the divinity in all living things. Most importantly however, it teaches responsibility. We accept responsibility for our actions and deeds as clearly a result of the choices we make… We acknowledge the cycles of nature, the lunar phases and the seasons to celebrate our spirituality and to worship the divine. It is a belief system that allows the witch to work with, not in supplication to deities with the intent of living in harmony and achieving balance with all things… The basis of Wicca is a simple statement called the Wiccan Rede. (Source: Wikipedia) “Eight words the Wiccan Rede fulfill, An it harm none do what ye will.” This is the first published form of the couplet, quoted from Doreen Valiente in 1964.

We have not found evidence that this “Rede” (as a whole) predates the 1950’s, so it is relatively new. The similar phrase “do as thou wilt” is originally found in a 16th century novel by François Rabelais: DO AS THOU WILT because men that are free of gentle birth, well bred and at home in civilized company possess a natural instinct that inclines them to virtue and saves them from vice. This instinct they name their honor.

To a Wiccan, the Rede does not mean they can just do whatever they want. We will expand on this later when we focus on the word “will,” meaning what it is I stand for; my internal focus, the expression of my being. (Source: https://www.wicca.com/wicca/what-is-wicca.html - What Wicca Is) …The spells that we do involve healing, love, harmony, wisdom and creativity. The potions that we stir might be a headache remedy, a cold tonic, or an herbal flea bath for our pets. We strive to gain knowledge of and use the natural remedies placed on this earth by the divine for our benefit instead of using synthetic drugs unless absolutely necessary… This indicates that Wiccans are about building up, being helpful and many good things come from these sources.

Magic and Christianity harmonize, Can You Be a Christian and a Witch, Owlvine Green - Any spirituality you have, any faith that you have, one billion percent can be put into the framework of magic; or rather, magic can come into that framework, since I feel like magic is something that's bigger. It’s something that’s within every culture and every tradition and every time; and in history, magic as we understand it now has been practiced in some form or another. Every religion. If you go back and look at folklore from the UK and places like that from a couple hundred years ago, you can see how, with Christian faith, they were practicing magic. So, they absolutely can get along together and they do harmonize.

Jesus never specifically talked about witchcraft – doesn’t that leave some room for interpretation?

Owlvine just gave us all kinds of interpretation! For instance, she said magic has been practiced by all religions through all historical times. The Jewish Law, for example, specifically forbade all kinds of witchcraft.

While Jesus did not directly comment on witchcraft in any form, we do have a set of verses that give a comprehensive list of what we should NOT do:

Deuteronomy 18:9-14: (NASB) 9When you enter the land which the LORD your God gives you, you shall not learn to imitate the detestable things of those nations. 10There shall not be found among you anyone who makes his son or his daughter pass through the fire, one who uses divination, one who practices witchcraft, or one who interprets omens, or a sorcerer, 11or one who casts a spell, or a medium, or a spiritist, or one who calls up the dead. 12For whoever does these things is detestable to the LORD; and because of these detestable things the LORD your God will drive them out before you. 13You shall be blameless before the LORD your God. 14For those nations, which you shall dispossess, listen to those who practice witchcraft and to diviners, but as for you, the LORD your God has not allowed you to do so.

These verses are important because there are several translations for each of these eight words or phrases.

Pagans often point to the differing translations to allege that the Bible is therefore unreliable on this point.

For whoever does these things is detestable to the LORD… but as for you, the LORD your God has not allowed you to do so – think of this as we review each item. This is not a “Well, maybe I can get away with it,” kind of list! The Jews were NOT to practice any kind of witchcraft.

We will show each word as it is translated in the New American Standard Version (1995), the New International Version (2011) and the King James Version.

Deuteronomy 18:10: (NASB) There shall not be found among you anyone who makes his son or his daughter pass through the fire, one who uses <7080> divination <7081> Uses: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance #7080 qacam; properly, to distribute, i.e. determine by lot or magical scroll; by implication, to divine

“Determine by lot” is a random method used to make a decision. In John 19:24, the soldiers guarding Jesus cast lots to determine who would get his clothes. In Ezekiel 21:21, Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, used marked arrows in a quiver to determine his next move. (He also examined entrails – specifically the liver - of a dead victim.)

The 11 apostles also cast lots to choose a replacement for Judas, but God ignored their actions. God's choice of the Apostle Paul became obvious.

One way Wicca and other Pagans today determine by lots is through randomly choosing and interpreting rune stones. Having a long ancient history, runes are tiles, stones or cards with carvings or letters that look like primitive markings. Each symbol of the alphabet has a special meaning and helps invoke the deities who can supposedly help you with your problems.

Scripturally, the word uses <7080> has one positive and many negative meanings, such as: God took away wise, competent rulers from Israel when they were sinful:

Isaiah 3:2: (KJV) The mighty man, and the man of war, the judge, and the prophet, and the prudent <7080>, and the ancient.

Jeremiah 29:8: (KJV) For thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Let not your prophets and your diviners <7080>, that be in the midst of you, deceive you, neither hearken to your dreams which ye cause to be dreamed.

Divination: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance #7081 qesem; a lot: also divination (including its fee), oracle Divination is using an object to gain answers or see events not perceptible by the average person. In ancient cultures, an oracle was a priest or priestess acting as a medium through whom advice or prophecy was sought from the gods. It can also refer to the response or message itself.

Wiccans are adamant that divination goes beyond mere fortune telling. One Wiccan website said, “Divination can provide you with divine guidance that allows you to make better choices and have a higher level of control over your future…It is like connecting with a wise old friend who can offer you divine guidance on anything and everything you want to talk about.”

Objects used include Tarot cards, crystal balls, pendulums or, as we just talked about, runes. There is also something called “bibliomancy.”

This uses a book, most often the Bible, to tell the future. A Wiccan opens the Bible and points to a random verse with their eyes closed. Upon opening their eyes, they provide a specialized interpretation or prediction. Old family Bibles are said to be especially powerful.

Do not do this at home! Do not take the holy Word of God and make it into a game! This practice shows no understanding of the sacredness of God’s word.

Scripturally, <7081> has one positive and many negative meanings, such as:

Proverbs 16:10: (KJV) A divine sentence <7081> is in the lips of the king: his mouth transgresseth not in judgment.

Jeremiah 14:14: (KJV) Then the LORD said unto me, The prophets prophesy lies in My name: I sent them not, neither have I commanded them, neither spake unto them: they prophesy unto you a false vision and divination <7081>, and a thing of nought, and the deceit of their heart. This is not something we should be doing – it is on the “never do list” from God Almighty. Those who do these things are not in harmony with Him.

There is a difference between the goodness someone does and the methods by which they are doing it. We have to be clear on this.

At first glance, the whole idea of white witchcraft seems fascinating and enticing. We need to find the rest of the story.

What exactly were the practices that God told Israel they absolutely had to avoid once in their promised land?

We have already seen that divination, seeking to know the future by some spiritual source other than God, was first on this list (aside from obviously not burning their children to false gods as live sacrifices - anyone who makes his son or his daughter pass through the fire). Having this instruction first sets the tone for the rest of the commands God told Israel not to do. After all, God was and is our source for anything and everything connected to spirituality. His word works as a unit, not as a randomly picked verse which someone pontificates.

In Part I, we talked about how Universalism - simply stated as all roads lead to heaven, no matter your path to get there – is NOT correct. This next audio clip from Owlvine Green suggests belief in Jesus is optional based on the path we feel is right for us.

It’s your path do what you will, Can You Be a Christian and a Witch, Owlvine Green

- It's your path. You do what you will, right? But that is the thing, as well, with everybody else’s path. If someone wants to bring in Christianity or they already are a Christian, or they want to bring Jesus in or whatever it is, that's okay to do. We're all on our own journey. We're all on our own soul path. And what we need to listen to is that voice within, that little guide that we have, those inclinations, all those callings that we have, or you just get sparked by something, and ooooh - you feel a draw towards something. Follow that. That is our inner guidance, and that never, I promise you, never leads us wrong, ever. And even if other people around us are saying this isn't right, this is the voice above all others that we should listen to. We take great objection to her statement!

Jeremiah 17:9: (KJV) The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?

Unless our conscience is hyper-trained to focus on God’s will, we cannot explicitly trust that we will always be drawn to the most God-honoring thoughts and actions.

Let’s examine the other practices forbidden by God’s specific instructions. For those who might say, “But this is the Old Testament, so it no longer applies,” we will see that Jesus often quoted from the Old Testament and believed it to be true.

Deuteronomy 18:10: (NASB) There shall not be found among you anyone who makes his son or his daughter pass through the fire, one who uses divination, one who practices witchcraft <6049>, or one who interprets omens, or a sorcerer, One who practices witchcraft: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance #6049`anan; to cover; to cloud over; figuratively, to act covertly, i.e. practice magic Witchcraft has historically been something practiced covertly, since many cultures throughout time invoked serious penalties for witchcraft, including making it punishable by death. Only recently has witchcraft, Wicca and Pagan practices in general, become more mainstream as society has become more accepting of everything and everyone’s personal desires. It has been normalized into our collective consciousness through television, movies and social media. But Wicca is still often a solitary practice or is practiced in small, secret covens of people.

It is often practiced at night because they want to draw the power or energy of the moon into their spells. Covertly literally means under the cover of darkness. There is a reason midnight is called the “witching hour.” Scripturally, <6049> has one positive use:

Genesis 9:14: (KJV) And it shall come to pass, when I bring <6049> a cloud over the earth, that the bow shall be seen in the cloud: All the other uses are about this covert practice in the darkness, such as:

Jeremiah 27:9: (KJV) Therefore hearken not ye to your prophets, nor to your diviners, nor to your dreamers, nor to your enchanters <6049>, nor to your sorcerers, which speak unto you, saying, Ye shall not serve the king of Babylon: I personally know several witches. With some of them, I have had conversations about witchcraft and Christianity. I have been told that the Old Testament does not apply to white witchcraft in this day and time. This is one of the reasons we are going through this so specifically. The Old Testament tells us these are practices that are condemned. It does not specify whether they are done for good or for bad reasons. If someone does this practice, they are out of harmony with God.

Jeremiah 10:23: (NASB1995) I know, O LORD, that a man's way is not in himself, nor is it in a man who walks to direct his steps.

In our last episode, we talked about many big-picture aspects of how humbling and amazing the privilege of prayer works. We learned that, as is usually the case with true Christian discipleship, there is much more to praying than talking to God about things and letting Him know what we need and want. Today we will focus on the details of our prayer life. We will look at many of those simple questions about the practicality of prayer. Questions like, how do we fit prayer into busy lives? How do we pray when we are not feeling grateful for anything? How do we know if God is answering our prayers or if we are just making up answers?

Transforming our prayer life requires us to have several biblical and fundamental truths in order regarding prayer. In Part I, we discussed several “Principles of Proper Prayer.” Let’s go further and begin by asking those important and practical “how” and “why” questions about praying with another fundamental truth:

A transformed prayer life is a mature prayer life, and this maturity does not just magically happen. It comes through thought, study, application and development. We have to grow up into a mature prayer life. Let’s examine several aspects of everyday prayer and see how we can work on this growing-up process.

Sometimes we pray based on fanciful or wishful thinking.

But what ARE we allowed to pray for? It seems like two people pray for the same thing, and one request randomly comes true and the other doesn’t - there’s no apparent rhyme or reason, for example, as to whose house stands after a natural disaster. We know God isn’t a magic genie granting our heart’s desires, so which of those desires are appropriate to ask for?

James 4:1-3: (NASB1995) 1What is the source of quarrels and conflicts among you? Is not the source your pleasures that wage war in your members? 2You lust and do not have; so you commit murder. You are envious and cannot obtain; so you fight and quarrel. You do not have because you do not ask. 3You ask and do not receive, because you ask with wrong motives, so that you may spend it on your pleasures.

In other words, you do not have because you do not ask, but when you do ask, it wasn’t the right question. What is too petty to bother God with? There must be millions of prayers a day going up to God to “Let me win the lottery so I can do really good things with the money.” What’s wrong with a prayer like that?

Instead of that prayer, we might ask, “Dear Father, let me NOT win the lottery so I can learn to do good things with what You have already given me.” It is all about perspective. God simply will not “hear” prayers that are just focused on us.

Instead of wishful thinking, let’s work on learning to pray in faith.

James 5:15-16: (NASB1995) 15and the prayer offered in faith will restore the one who is sick, and the Lord will raise him up, and if he has committed sins, they will be forgiven him. 16Therefore, confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another so that you may be healed. The effective prayer of a righteous man can accomplish much.

Confess your sins to one another – be vulnerable. This can be scary and difficult in a group of people. There is always a danger in having the mistakes we shared in confidence turn into gossip or judgment. Wolves in sheep’s clothing can take advantage of our weaknesses. We must be surrounded by those we trust who live their lives with appropriateness and godliness when we are requesting prayers on our behalf.

If you are not in the right company, find a proper spiritual environment. Instead of praying wishfully, pray in faith. In every prayer we want to grow in maturity – in the direction of true faith - and not just wishful thinking.

Sometimes as we pray and look for God’s leadings, thoughts pop into our heads. - How do we know which thoughts are our own and which thoughts are God’s? These random thoughts seem sensible – is that God speaking to me? Is He answering prayer? - If I follow through on those thoughts, am I doing God’s will?

The following text is not about prayer, but it illustrates the process of the human mind. Jesus told a profound parable about a rich man whose wealth is increasing because his land is productive. He decides he will handle his increased wealth by building bigger barns to hold all of his crops. This may seem reasonable.

Luke 12:16-21: (NASB1995) 16And he told them a parable, saying, The land of a rich man was very productive. 17And he began reasoning to himself, saying, What shall I do, since I have no place to store my crops? 18Then he said, this is what I will do: I will tear down my barns and build larger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods. 19And I will say to my soul, Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years to come; take your ease, eat, drink and be merry. 20But God said to him, you fool! This very night your soul is required of you; and now who will own what you have prepared? 21So is the man who stores up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.

Instead of trusting the thoughts in our head, we need to pause and consider if these thoughts are in line with God’s word, holy principles and our living a life of selfless discipleship. Our focus should be on asking in humility and not telling God what we want His answer to be.

Luke 12:29-31: (NASB1995) 29And do not seek what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not keep worrying. 30For all these things the nations of the world eagerly seek; but your Father knows that you need these things. 31But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added to you.

In our prayer process, many thoughts and potential answers come into our heads. Are these based on God’s word, His holy principles and my living selflessly as a disciple? These are good gateways for our thought process before we consider moving forward. We need to question and re-question our own potential willfulness and stubbornness if we are seeking God’s answers and not our own desires.

We are willful people – that’s human nature in a sinful state. We should always question our motives when we are seeking God’s will:

Psalms 32:8-10: (NASB1995) 8I will instruct you and teach you in the way which you should go; I will counsel you with My eye upon you. 9Do not be as the horse or as the mule which have no understanding, whose trappings include bit and bridle to hold them in check, otherwise they will not come near to you. 10Many are the sorrows of the wicked, but he who trusts in the LORD, lovingkindness shall surround him.

God says, I will instruct you and teach you in the way which you should go. Do not be as the horse or mule who need to have a bit in their mouth and a bridal so that they can be pushed and pulled in the direction they are to go. When we want God’s answers to our prayers to be what WE want them to be, we are looking at our personal preference versus God’s providence.

In the big scheme of things, do we want our personal preference to be the answer, or do we want God’s eternal providence? It comes down to our preference versus God's will and His providence.

We can fabricate an answer inside our own mind, thoughts and heart that feels right. But if it is not based in godly principle, in selflessness, in God’s holy word, then how can it be right in God’s eyes? God’s eyes are what count. When we think we have received answers to prayer, the first question we have to ask ourselves is whether our answer is in accordance with God’s will.

I have had the great privilege to work with many individuals with all kinds of challenges in life. One of my biggest fears in those experiences is ME. I am afraid to get in the way of the Lord’s words – that my words will come out rather than the Lord’s words working through me. For me, it takes labor to make sure I am responding, not reacting, on a scriptural basis, a spiritual basis, a brotherhood basis, or a “lifting someone up” basis rather than me saying, “I can tell you a thing or two.”

Am I hearing me because it is really convenient to get what I want because I am answering? Or am I hearing my heavenly Father’s providence unfold in a scripturally- sound, spiritually-mature way? We are just getting started and already we can see how easy it can be to customize our prayer life to be self-serving instead of God honoring!

Does how we present ourselves in prayer matter?

How about the role our feelings play? How should we pray regarding our future? When looking to transform our prayer lives, we need to accept that everything matters, and no aspect of our prayers should be taken lightly. We need to continually remind ourselves that when we go to God through Jesus, we are not telling Him anything He doesn’t know, but we are presenting ourselves before the God of ALL! When we go to Him through Christ, He already knows. We need to remember that as we go through these practicalities of our prayer life. What is our next potential challenge? When we learn to pray as a child, we learn formulaic phrases that are helpful to teach us a pattern, but at some point these might keep us from building an actual relationship with God.

Sometimes we pray, making sure we hit all the right words or phrases that might make us look humble. To those hearing us, we openly acknowledge righteousness and appropriate desires. It’s a little like putting on a mask.

Luke 18:9-12: (NASB1995) 9And he also told this parable to some people who trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and viewed others with contempt: 10Two men went up into the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector. 11The Pharisee stood and was praying this to himself: God, I thank you that I am not like other people: swindlers, unjust, adulterers, or even like this tax collector. 12I fast twice a week; I pay tithes of all that I get. The Pharisee was basically using a checklist: I pay my tithes.

I fast.

I’m ritually working hard at fulfilling what You gave me to do.

This Pharisee believed in his own presentation of evidence, but his heart was wrong. We can modernize this idea, especially in the world of social media where it’s reinforced that we have to look and act a certain way. Perception is everything. It has nothing to do with what’s in our hearts or any kind of godly transformation. But it sure looks good! Instead of wearing a mask, pray in sincere and genuine humility as we cling to righteousness and godliness.

Luke 18:13-14: (NASB1995) 13But the tax collector, standing some distance away, was even unwilling to lift up his eyes to heaven, but was beating his breast, saying, God, be merciful to me, the sinner!

Here’s how Jesus responded: 14I tell you, this man went to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but he who humbles himself will be exalted.

This is the opposite of looking good. The tax collector was all about being acceptable to God, so his prayer was acceptable. He was honest and vulnerable.

On the one hand, the Pharisee was looking for just the right words and the right presentation: “I thank God for my maturity,” versus the tax collector’s, “I am not worthy.” The best of us at the highest spirituality in our lives are still not worthy! We still have absolutely zero worthiness before God. Our ability to come before our Father is because we wear that robe of Christ’s righteousness. We go to God through Christ. This is what brings us the worthiness to approach God.

Christian maturity is not an exercise of comparison. It is not about the appropriateness of this, that or the other thing. It is about growing into the appropriate lifestyle, the appropriate actions, the appropriate thoughts and the appropriate heart.

Sometimes we pray based on passing thoughts or feelings that impulsively make us want something that isn’t well thought out.

Ecclesiastes 5:1-2: (NASB1995) 1Guard your steps as you go to the house of God and draw near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools; for they do not know they are doing evil. 2Do not be hasty in word or impulsive in thought to bring up a matter in the presence of God…

Our minds are very active. Most times it will bring us to the wrong direction or conclusion if left unchecked. However, does the admonition not to be impulsive conflict with how we are supposed to be instant in prayer or constant in prayer? There is a lot to think about when we think about thinking, and we then translate that to prayers before the Almighty! While an impulsive thought may be a good way to begin prayer, let’s instead work towards praying with diligent focus and attention, knowing that God can and will work in our lives.

…For God is in heaven and you are on the earth; therefore let your words be few. The wandering, active practice of our minds might be a good way to START prayer. However, let that active seeking bring us to a place of pausing, considering and slowing down – so that the racing of our humanity can begin to give space to listening to God’s perspective.

Prayer is not just about talking; it is about putting things before the LORD in a selah moment –pause and consider – to help put our thoughts in order. We do not want the racing of our own minds to be in the way of prayer. If that is how we start a prayer, wonderful, but see if we can guide it into something higher.

Let’s observe and learn from the humble petitioning of one of God’s faithful servants in the Old Testament.

Daniel was in Babylon for YEARS and prayed for the return of Israel to their home:

Daniel 9:17-19: (NASB1995) 17So now, our God, listen to the prayer of Your servant and to his supplications, and for Your sake, O Lord, let Your face shine on Your desolate sanctuary. 18O my God, incline Your ear and hear! Open Your eyes and see our desolations and the city which is called by Your name; for we are not presenting our supplications before You on account of any merits of our own, but on account of Your great compassion. 19O Lord, hear! O Lord, forgive! O Lord, listen and take action! For Your own sake, O my God, do not delay, because Your city and Your people are called by Your name.

Daniel says Your twelve times in these two verses! Why? This is because it is about the will of God and about honoring God.

Daniel was assured by prophecy that Israel would be restored to their land. He knew their captivity would end. His prayer reflected his obedience to God’s will and reverence for God’s honor. His prayers had focus and purpose. Daniel asked God not to hesitate bringing these things to be, even though he knew these events would not happen for a long time. Why?

Fervent prayer like this - even when we know a situation is a long-term issue - is an expression of true reverence because we are putting our heart before God, laying out how we think it will be solved today – knowing full well it will not be – but saying, “LORD, do not hesitate because Your will is so important to me.” That is reverence! Racing thoughts could race us into reverent behavior. Daniel shows this by taking his racing thought and focusing it on God’s will, His way and His providence.
